381YE Winter Solstice Imperial elections.d: Most senators were returned or newly elected. Redoubt's senator resigned, Volodmartz's was revoked and Semmerholm's was murdered, and all three were replaced. Zenith's incumbent held the seat until the territory fell to barbarian orcs. Generals were confirmed or replaced, including after battlefield deaths in the Bounders and the Army of the Golden Axe. The Synod filled cardinal, inquisitor and other posts, and the Cardinal of Pride abdicated. Conclave archmages and grandmasters were chosen, and Bourse seats and ministries were auctioned or won by vote. No appointments were made for the Dean of Pilgrims, the Imperial Master of Works or the Crystal Architect. The Druj destroyed four Zenith titles and Grendel destroyed the Freeborn Storm.

n.Dawn: Bohemond de Rondell kept Astolat's Senate seat, and Lady Ailliena Devereux replaced Semmerholm's murdered senator.
n.Druj: Druj action in Zenith destroyed the Custodian of the Starlight Drift, the Keeper of the Tower of the Fall, the Custodian of the Storm Vault and Origen's Rest.
n.Grendel: Grendel action in Madruga destroyed the Freeborn Storm title.
n.Highguard: Jeconiah of Ravens Watch was elected senator for Necropolis.
n.Imperial Orcs: Irontide Vio was returned as senator for Skarsind, and Atla of the Imperial Orcs remained Cardinal of the Way.
n.Navarr: Rhisiart Dancewalker was elected senator for Hercynia.
n.The Brass Coast: Adan i Del-Tero i Riqueza became senator for Madruga, while the Freeborn Storm title there was destroyed by Grendel.
n.The League: Gant Archama was returned as senator for Temeschwar.
n.The Marches: Orrick Bolholt was returned as senator for Bregasland.
n.Urizen: Andronikos replaced Redoubt's resigning senator, and Zenith was lost to barbarian orcs, with four of its titles destroyed. Urizen's senators presented no unanimous choice for Crystal Architect of the Spires, though Solas of Urizen remained High Exorcist and Alcuin Shatterspire Head Gardener of Urizen.
n.Varushka: Father Nikolovich Drakov kept Miekarova, and Alexei Volostra replaced Volodmartz's revoked senator. After the Army of the Golden Axe's general died in battle, the Varushkan senators presented no unanimous replacement.
n.Wintermark: Edythe Dunne was elected senator for Kallavesa. Wintermark citizens also took the posts of Fallsheart Guardian (Breeta Dunning), Master Apothecary (Kai Dunning) and Virtue Inquisitor of the Way (Yarrick Ursan).

t.Astolat: Bohemond de Rondell was returned as Astolat's senator.
t.Bregasland: Orrick Bolholt was returned as Bregasland's senator.
t.Hercynia: Rhisiart Dancewalker was elected senator for Hercynia.
t.Kallavesa: Edythe Dunne was elected senator for Kallavesa.
t.Madruga: Adan i Del-Tero i Riqueza was elected Madruga's senator, and Grendel destroyed the Freeborn Storm title there.
t.Miekarova: Father Nikolovich Drakov was returned as senator for Miekarova.
t.Necropolis: Jeconiah of Ravens Watch was elected senator for Necropolis.
t.Redoubt: Redoubt's senator resigned and was replaced by Andronikos.
t.Semmerholm: Semmerholm's senator was murdered and replaced by Lady Ailliena Devereux.
t.Skarsind: Irontide Vio was returned as senator for Skarsind.
t.Temeschwar: Gant Archama was returned as Temeschwar's senator.
t.Volodmartz: Volodmartz's senator was revoked and replaced by Alexei Volostra.
t.Zenith: The incumbent senator served until Zenith was lost to barbarian orcs, and the Druj destroyed four titles there, including the Custodian of the Storm Vault and Origen's Rest.

381YE Winter Solstice Senate sessions.d: Passed motions included new ambassadors to Axos and Faraden, a general for the Strong Reeds, the Senate power of escalation, construction of mana exchanges in Temeschwar and Sarvos, the walls of Holberg, a gate in Semmerholm, Lorenzo's Legacy works, and funds for the Wintermark army. The Mournwold thralls were declared foreigners and the Verthandi spy network decommissioned. Amending the Advisor on the Vallorn's powers, the power of relinquishment and an arsenal in Sarvos failed. The Throne vetoed the Arcane Architect's summer mana sinecure in Reikos. Imperatrix Lisabetta exercised the Hand of the Chancellor for 473 thrones and announced an address to the Empire; 11 commissions were announced.

n.Highguard: The Arcane Architect's planned summer mana sinecure in Highguard-held Reikos was vetoed by the Throne, so it will not go ahead there.
n.Wintermark: The Senate passed a motion to disburse funds for the Wintermark army.

t.Reikos: A summer mana sinecure the Arcane Architect announced for Reikos was vetoed by the Throne, leaving the territory without it.

381YE Winter Solstice winds of fortune.d: The page indexed many events. A Synod judgement produced mandates to encourage the Way, and Jarm saw slave reforms and an offer of beloye zerno. Dawn kept Semmerholm despite losing Axmure and its Gate. The Winter Sun experimented with the relic Defiance in Casinea. Escaped slaves raided Kalino from Feroz. Orc former-thralls and resentful Mournwolders sought redress. The Liathaven vallorn threatened West Ranging. The Grendel turned on the trading fleet, and a great storm reshaped northern Varushka. The Blood Red Roads were completed, Zemress exiles settled in Segura, the Jotun dismantled the Hordalant spy network, and five Synod mandates were upheld.

n.Dawn: Dawn did not lose Semmerholm to the Druj despite the fall of Axmure and its Gate, and fervour swept the nation as its boast of never losing a territory to barbarians held.
n.Druj: Having taken Axmure and destroyed the Gate the season before, the Druj failed to complete the conquest of Semmerholm.
n.Grendel: After the destruction of the Freeborn Storm, the Grendel effectively dominate the Bay of Catazar, and their pirates, urged on by Siakha, now target the Imperial trading fleet. Interest is growing in locating them along the Bay.
n.Highguard: The Heirs of Lepidus showed that the Silent Sentinel is likely the dwelling of the paragon the Sentinel, offering a chance to celebrate it. A Highguard mandate rejecting the Land without Tears will heal the Yaelian Schism.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Winter Sun used the relic Defiance in an experimental ritual in Casinea. Imperial Orcs are also concerned with the orc former-thralls left in the Mournwold, and they chose the heroic path in the debate over cruelty and fear.
n.Jotun: The Jotun have fled the Mournwold, leaving many orc former-thralls behind, and over the season they dismantled the Hordalant spy network.
n.Navarr: The Liathaven vallorn threatens to consume West Ranging, a Navarr mandate sent herbs to aid the orcs of Therunin, and Navarr magicians were among those affected by the flood of Spring magic.
n.The Brass Coast: Some two hundred escaped slaves have camped in southern Feroz and are raiding Kalino. The Zemress exiles are settling in Segura, and a mandate will improve the quality of the Red Wind Corsairs.
n.The League: The League completed the Blood Red Roads, the Grand Park of Holberg and red stone mana monoliths in all four of its territories, inspiring its people. A potent new street drug has also appeared.
n.The Marches: With the Jotun gone, Mournwolders sent three representatives to Anvil seeking recompense, and the fate of the remaining orc former-thralls is unresolved. Strange mists bring fecund short-lived plants to Bregasland, and Feni raid Upwold.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Thule in Otkodov are named as one of three orc nations with recent developments in their relations with the Empire.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Urizen is among the nations tagged as interested in the return and flood of Spring regio power.
n.Varushka: A once-in-a-century storm reshaped the northern mountains of Varushka, opening four opportunities to build from the destruction. The Varushkans also have a chance to answer the Imperial Orcs in the debate over cruelty and fear.
n.Wintermark: A Wintermark mandate will change its armies' tactics for four seasons to seek heroic victory over the Jotun rather than slaughter, while drowned dead appeared in Sermersuaq and Feni raided Hahnmark.

t.Bay of Catazar: The Grendel now effectively dominate the Bay, contested only by a few Imperial captains, and their pirates are turning on the trading fleet.
t.Bregasland: Eerie mists are bringing farmers the seeds of peculiar short-lived plants rich with fecund power.
t.Casinea: The Winter Sun spent the season here resupplying and performing an experimental ritual with the relic Defiance to seek a stronger connection with their ancestors.
t.Feroz: Around two hundred escaped slaves fleeing Duke Guiscard have built makeshift camps in southern Feroz and are raiding across the border into Kalino.
t.Hahnmark: Feni raiders have struck Hahnmark, linked to conjunctions of the Sentinel Gate.
t.Holberg: The long-delayed Grand Park of Holberg was completed, red stone monoliths now enhance its mana, and the Blood Red Roads connect it to the other League cities.
t.Hordalant: The Jotun dismantled the Hordalant spy network, and no military unit can be assigned to it any longer.
t.Kalino: Revolutionaries camped in Feroz are making periodic raids across the border into Kalino, creating a complex diplomatic situation with the Iron Confederacy.
t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: Karov is not named directly, though the storm that reshaped the northern mountains of Varushka is relevant to Varushkan lands.
t.Liathaven: The vallorn of Liathaven is moving and shifting, and if nothing is done it will consume all of West Ranging.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: Madruga is not named directly, appearing only through Brass Coast matters such as the mandate improving the Red Wind Corsairs.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: the Blood Red Roads have been extended to Holt in Miaren.
t.Mournwold: The Jotun have fled, but many orc former-thralls remain. Mournwolders still resentful of the magic used against the Jotun sent representatives to Anvil to seek recompense.
t.Otkodov: The Thule of Otkodov are among the orc nations whose relations with the Empire saw recent developments.
t.Sarvos: A collision struck Sarvos, linked to a conjunction of the Sentinel Gate. Red stone monoliths to enhance mana flows were also completed there.
t.Segura: Exiles from the Isle of Zemress have been establishing a home in Segura and are expected to be settled by the Spring Equinox.
t.Semmerholm: After losing Axmure and the Gate, Semmerholm did not fall to the Druj, and its survival sparked fervour across Dawn.
t.Sermersuaq: Drowned dead have appeared in Sermersuaq, linked to a conjunction of the Sentinel Gate.
t.Tassato: Mana-enhancing red stone monoliths were completed here, bearing the controversial personal stamp of the Asavean architect Almodin Oktístis.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar's monoliths, honouring Lorenzo Macelliao von Temeschwar, were completed with Almodin Oktístis's controversial touches, and the Blood Red Roads link it to the other League cities.
t.Therunin: The Great Forest Orcs in Therunin received aid through a Navarr mandate urging apothecaries and physicks to share spare herbs with them.
t.Upwold: Feni raiders struck Upwold among other territories, linked to conjunctions of the Sentinel Gate.

r.Liathaven/West Ranging: The shifting Liathaven vallorn will consume all of West Ranging unless something is done before its aberrant vitality subsides.
r.Miaren/Holtford: Mentioned in passing: the Blood Red Roads were extended to Holt in Miaren.
r.Semmerholm/Axmure: Axmure, conquered by the Druj the previous season with the Gate destroyed, was the base for their push deeper into Semmerholm, which ultimately failed.

381YE Winter Solstice winds of war.d: A Druj marshwalker broke the Golden Cascade dam, ruining Zenith's farms. The Druj burned the Arch of the Sky and now hold nine-tenths of Proceris. Four Dawnish armies, nine thousand Summer knights and the Fist of the Mountains pushed the Druj into southern Axmure at a cost of some eight thousand casualties on both sides. The Jotun abandoned Mournwold entirely. In Spiral, Imperial armies made headway in Screed, but the Grendel kept the region and the Black Plateau drove soldiers to madness and suicide. The Grendel armada burned the Atalaya shipyard and the Freeborn Storm, and took Free Landing and eastern Lightsea. The civil service identified Sentinel Gate conjunctions for the coming summit.

n.Dawn: All four Dawnish armies fought together for the first time in over a century and, with three cohorts of Summer knights, drove the Druj back into southern Axmure. Some four and a half thousand Imperial citizens were lost in the campaign.
n.Druj: The Druj flooded Proceris and now hold nine-tenths of it, leaving Zenith on the brink. In Semmerholm they were pushed back to southern Axmure, though the Black Wind's atrocities and a guerrilla force in Ulvenholm remain.
n.Grendel: The Grendel armada destroyed the Freeborn Storm, took Free Landing and eastern Lightsea, and claimed the Bay of Catazar. In Screed the Grendel defended cautiously and kept control, and they fortified the port at Apulus.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Druj slaughtered as many Imperial Orcs at Estcastle as they could find, and the survivors sheltered in the Frozen Citadel. A large force of Imperial Orc reavers supported the Wolves of War in Screed.
n.Jotun: The Jotun retreated entirely from Mournwold, tearing down Hillstop as they went. Elite kirkja bands, the Ice Fishers of Ldansk in Sermersuaq and a flame-bird host in Segura, appear to be preparing the way for invasion.
n.Navarr: The Quiet Step, accompanied by vates and strange supernatural creatures, helped complete the liberation of Mournwold. The Black Thorns were severely mauled trying to defend Atalaya and Quzar, and the beacon at Rest was lit to warn of the Jotun in Sermersuaq.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn lost the Freeborn Storm, the Atalaya shipyard and the birthplace of their nation, as well as Quzar and Midport, and their admiral lost the title. Meanwhile the Fire of the South and the Red Wind Corsairs fought and raided in Screed, and Jotun warriors entered Yellow Chase.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the Towerjacks withdrew toward Sarvos to resupply, and some League captains in Screed fell back in disarray, gripped by the Black Plateau's delusions.
n.The Marches: Marcher armies freed the last of the Mournwold, including old Sarcombe, and the Drakes were able to resupply from Mitwold. The political mood in the Mourn remains tense, with the Singing Caves still unallocated by the Senate.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Senate's peace with the Thule three years earlier is cited as the reason Sermersuaq had been relatively quiet.
n.Urizen: Urizen lost the Golden Cascade, the Arch of the Sky and several sinecures in Zenith, and Zenith's farms now suffer reduced production. In Spiral the Citadel Guard, aided by Axou skirmishers, pressed into Screed but could not take it.
n.Wintermark: The Fist of the Mountains protected western Semmerholm but was hammered by Druj flank attacks. The Green Shield's husks grew vicious in Screed, and the Ice Fishers of Ldansk began preparing for an invasion of Sermersuaq.

t.Bay of Catazar: The Shining Pillar now burns purple, signalling that the Bay belongs to the Grendel. A hypnotic fog off the Spiral coast is crippling the production of any fleet based in Spiral.
t.Brocéliande: Druj scouts from Ulvenholm probed south into the northern forest but retreated as soon as they saw the steadings' defensive thorns.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the Black Wind led a Druj push toward the Semmerlak and Holberg.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: the Quiet Step passed through Kahraman to collect supplies provided by the Spider King, and the Cinnamon Road runs north to it.
t.Kalino: Mentioned in passing: Iron Confederacy soldiers from Kalino fought alongside Dawn, and the cleared pass into Reinos opens a road between Kalino and Segura.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun appear to have learned from their failed attempts to invade Kallavesa.
t.Liathaven: The last Jotun from Southmoor fell back into Liathaven. A Sentinel Gate conjunction to Mournstead offers the Navarr a chance to engage two of their hated enemies there.
t.Madruga: The Grendel took all of Free Landing and the eastern coast of Lightsea, burning the Atalaya shipyard and sacking Quzar, which cut Madruga's taxation. Siroc remains untouched for now.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: the Drakes drew on the wealth of Mitwold to rearm and re-equip.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: many refugees from Zenith moved north into Morrow seeking shelter.
t.Mournwold: Mournwold is now entirely under Marcher and Imperial control, though its people are uneasy. The civil service is examining whether Hillstop, the Tribute and Orchard's Watch can be rebuilt.
t.Redoubt: Because the Crow Road pass was held open, Imperial armies could move through Redoubt to and from Spiral, and two Freeborn armies marched south through it.
t.Reinos: The landslip blocking the pass over Old Man's Ride from Reinos into Segura was cleared and the road repaired. A planned conjunction aims to force the invaders back into Reinos.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: the Towerjacks withdrew toward Sarvos to resupply, and a messenger from Glass Point warned of the Grendel armada.
t.Segura: Between one and two thousand Jotun warriors with Lasambrian ties are fortifying an old bandit camp in Yellow Chase. A conjunction offers a chance to drive them out.
t.Semmerholm: The Druj were halted and pushed back into southern Axmure after two months of bloody fighting, but they still hold the region and threaten Ulvenholm.
t.Sermersuaq: An elite Jotun force of around fifteen hundred warriors is building bridges, fortifications and supply caches in Stark to prepare for invasion, and the beacon at Rest has been lit.
t.Skallahn: Mentioned in passing: Winterfolk who accept the Jotun Choice are reportedly sent west to Tromsa, Skallahn and beyond.
t.Spiral: Imperial armies pushed deep into Screed while holding their gains in Ankra, but the Grendel kept control and the Black Plateau grew stronger. The Grendel also fortified Apulus.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun hall at Sarcombe once kept watch east toward Tassato.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: the Black Wind were once free orcs of the Barrens before returning to the Druj.
t.The Semmerlak: Mentioned in passing: the Black Wind led the Druj force pushing toward the Semmerlak.
t.Tromsa: Mentioned in passing: captives who accept the Choice are reportedly sent west to Tromsa.
t.Zenith: A catastrophic flood ruined the Golden Cascade and the Druj destroyed several sinecures. The Druj now hold almost all of Proceris, and one more victory would give them Zenith.

r.Brocéliande/Boar's Dell: The Navarr of Boar's Dell reported Druj scouts from Ulvenholm crossing the border, apparently searching for something, before they withdrew.
r.Liathaven/Liath's Ring: A smaller conjunction will open to Mournstead, an old steading near the vallorn miasma, for a large skirmish against Navarr enemies that also concerns the Freeborn.
r.Liathaven/Liaven's Glen: Mentioned in passing: the Quiet Step's orders spoke of carving a new road to Liaven's Glen.
r.Madruga/Calvos Sound: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel armada bypassed Calvos Sound on its way to Free Landing.
r.Madruga/Free Landing: The whole region fell to the Grendel, including the Shining Pillar, Atalaya and Midport. The shipyard and the Freeborn Storm were burnt to the waterline.
r.Madruga/Lightsea: The Grendel conquered Lightsea's eastern coast and sacked the rich port of Quzar despite the Black Thorns' resistance, and are close to claiming the whole region.
r.Mournwold/Green March: Green March was freed as the last Jotun warbands withdrew, leaving behind only a few stubborn human and orc thralls.
r.Mournwold/Greensward: Mentioned in passing: the Quiet Step marched up through the Greensward to join the liberation.
r.Mournwold/Southmoor: Southmoor, the last region lost to the Jotun, was the last to be freed. Old Sarcombe was liberated as a ruin after the Jotun tore down Hillstop.
r.Redoubt/Willstone: The Crow Road pass linking Willstone and Cinion was kept open, allowing Imperial armies to resupply and reinforce Spiral.
r.Segura/Yellow Chase: Jotun warriors under a flame-bird banner reoccupied the old Lasambrian camp and are raising a palisade. A conjunction to Madera Viejo offers a chance to strike at them.
r.Semmerholm/Axmure: The Gryphon's Pride smashed the Druj defences, and the Druj now hold southern Axmure only tenuously. The region's woods are strewn with the dead.
r.Semmerholm/Estmure: The Druj assaulted Estcastle and damaged Lacre's cathedral, but a Frozen Citadel sheltered the defenders, and the Dawnish charge drove the orcs back after bloody fighting.
r.Semmerholm/Ulvenholm: A lizard-banner Druj force with Vikari made for the Pits of Brychel and a guerrilla force remains. A conjunction to the Chase of Arnet offers a chance to engage it.
r.Sermersuaq/Stark: The Ice Fishers of Ldansk are preparing an invasion route through Stark and camp a day from Rest. A conjunction to Kugaaruk Point offers a chance to engage them.
r.Spiral/Ankra: Imperial gains in Ankra have not been compromised so far, although the Grendel used it to flank the advance into Screed.
r.Spiral/Apulus: The Grendel rebuilt and heavily fortified the port with a castle raised at almost supernatural speed, and ships berthed there are protected from the coastal magic.
r.Spiral/Ateri: The Grendel concentrated forces in Ateri and used it to flank the Imperial advance after Imperial troops were withdrawn from there.
r.Spiral/Cinion: Cinion, at the far end of the Crow Road, served as the gathering point where the Freeborn armies rejoined the main Imperial force.
r.Spiral/Ossuary: The Fire of the South and the Red Wind Corsairs broke out of northern Ossuary. Imperial forces kept minor gains there while Grendel forces remain concentrated in the region.
r.Spiral/Screed: The Empire fought its first major campaign in Screed, taking Grendel camps but not the region, while the waking Black Plateau drove both sides to madness and suicide. A conjunction to Fulgentius' Solitary is planned.
r.Zenith/Clypion: The Granite Pillar's vigilance kept the Druj in Clypion to small bands of scouts and assassins, and the Highborn still hold it.
r.Zenith/Iteri: Iteri, shielded by Clypion, remained relatively safe, but its spires are overcrowded with refugees whom the Valiant Pegasus are housing in makeshift camps.
r.Zenith/Lustri: The Druj consolidated their hold on Lustri, and many of its fleeing refugees were caught by the flood or by the orcs.
r.Zenith/Occursion: The Druj tightened their grip on Occursion as its refugees fled west into the floodwaters.
r.Zenith/Proceris: The Golden Cascade was destroyed by flood, the Arch of the Sky was burned, and the Druj now hold nine-tenths of the region. A conjunction to the Plantation of Tall Ferns could stop monstrous Druj reinforcements.

All work together.d: Nina's Summer 381YE judgement implied a mandate, but the civil service treated it as a statement of principle and sent it to every priest. Five mandates followed, each sending a priest with 100 liao to preach. Nina's and Bartimaeus's orthodox mandates would have strengthened the Highguard, Varushkan and League congregations at the expense of the Marches, Brass Coast and Wintermark. Bartimaeus's and Jorma Steelhail's also risked vigilante persecution of heretics, foreigners or the unvirtuous. Brother Orchard's would have reversed the orthodox balance. Several were upheld, but Severin's unity mandate won. It favoured no congregation and strongly inhibits attempts to stir religious conflict for a year.

n.Dawn: Past doubts about Dawn's orthodoxy were said to be somewhat eased by Viviane de Couerdefer's statement that glory lies through true Virtue. Dawn's congregations would not have been affected by any of the proposed mandates.
n.Highguard: Highguard was named among the most orthodox nations, and Bartimaeus of the Shattered Tower proposed the strident anti-heresy mandate. Because the unity mandate prevailed, Highborn congregations gained none of the liao or votes the orthodox mandates would have brought.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs were described as having found a place in the Way through the recent doctrinal changes of the Yaelian Schism. They would not have been affected by any of the mandates.
n.Navarr: The Navarr were described as accepting Virtue through their own Great Dance, a philosophy not greatly at odds with the Way. Their congregations were unaffected by the mandates.
n.The Marches: The Marches were named among the least orthodox nations, for beliefs such as rebirth as apple trees or rats and passing unvirtuous acts to others. Brother Orchard's heterodox mandate would have boosted Marcher congregations, but the unity mandate's success spared them both loss and gain.
n.Urizen: The Urizen were described as approaching Virtue through the Net of the Heavens, which is not particularly at odds with the Way. Their congregations were unaffected by the mandates.
n.Varushka: Varushka was counted among the most orthodox nations and would have gained congregation strength under the orthodox mandates, or lost it under Brother Orchard's. The unity mandate left its congregations unchanged.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's heroic veneration and swamp burials put it among the least orthodox nations, which the orthodox mandates would have weakened. Jorma Steelhail of Wintermark proposed the mandate to persecute the unvirtuous, but the unity mandate prevailed instead.

t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: the historical Abbot Robin of Upwold is cited for his rejected early-Empire claim that the Labyrinth of Ages was a metaphor for a soul's time as a tree.

Archive:381YE Winter Solstice Imperial t.d: The register named every senator except Temeschwar's, which was vacant. It also listed Senate advisors, ambassadors, sinecures and ministries, and the generals of the Military Council. Varushka's Army of the Golden Axe had no general after the death of Volk Kunzetsov Strascovih, so his adjutant was carrying out the general's duties. The Synod's cardinals, gatekeepers and virtue inquisitors, the Conclave's Archmagi and Grandmasters, and the Bourse seats with their winning bids were all recorded. The Singing Caves awaited allocation by the Senate. Two national Bourse positions were held by foreigners: Wintermark's Stonefield Ice Caves by the Thule and Urizen's Legacy by the Grendel. Three Imperial wayleaves were auctioned for one season.

n.Dawn: Dawn held three Senate seats and four generalships: the Hounds of Glory, Golden Sun, Eastern Sky and Gryphon's Pride. Its people also held the Cardinal of Ambition, Viviane de Coeurdefer, the Cardinal of Wisdom, Abaddon De Rondell, and the High Bard, Kaywenn du Launcet.
n.Grendel: The Grendel held The Legacy, a Urizen national Bourse position.
n.Highguard: Highguard held four Senate seats and the generalships of the Seventh Wave, Granite Pillar and Valiant Pegasus. Its people also held several virtue inquisitor posts and Conclave offices, including Bursar of the Conclave and Penumbral Watcher.
n.Imperial Orcs: Irontide Vio sat for Skarsind, while Bloodcrow Morg'ur and Irontide Skar led the Winter Sun and Summer Storm. Atla was Cardinal of the Way and Bloodcrow Ergot was Chaplain Consular, but the orcs' Brilliant Shore Bourse seat stood vacant.
n.Navarr: Navarr held three Senate seats and the generalships of the Black Thorns and Quiet Step. Its people were also Warmage (Heilyn of Bronwen's Rest) and Quartermaster General (Brendan Brackensong).
n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast held all four of its Senate seats and the generalships of the Red Wind Corsairs and Fire of the South. Esteban i Del Rio Blanco i Guerra was Imperial Fleet Master.
n.The League: The Throne was held by a Leaguer, Empress Lisabetta Giacomi von Holberg, but Temeschwar's Senate seat was vacant. Leaguers led the Wolves of War and Towerjacks, held the Cardinals of Pride and Vigilance, and served as Imperial Consul and Dean of the Academy.
n.The Marches: The Marches filled all four Senate seats and four generalships: the Tusks, Drakes, Strong Reeds and Bounders. Martin Orchard was Imperial Inquisitor and Mel Greenhill was Conscience of the Senate.
n.Thule: The Thule held the Stonefield Ice Caves, a Wintermark national Bourse position.
n.Urizen: Urizen held two Senate seats and the generalship of the Citadel Guard under Nicassia Avicia of Phoenix Reach. Urizeni also served as High Exorcist and Seer of the Gateway, while the nation's Legacy Bourse seat was held by the Grendel.
n.Varushka: Varushka held four Senate seats, but the Army of the Golden Axe had no general after Volk Kunzetsov Strascovih's death, and his adjutant was carrying out the duties. Varushkans also served as Dean of the Lyceum and Imperial Magus.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark held three Senate seats, the generalships of the Green Shield and Fist of the Mountain, and the Cardinals of Courage and Loyalty. Its Stonefield Ice Caves Bourse seat was held by the Thule.

t.Astolat: Bohemond de Rondell was Senator for Astolat.
t.Bastion: Sammual, of the Cohort of the Winter Bear, was Senator for Bastion.
t.Bregasland: Orrick Bolholt was Senator for Bregasland, the Dour Fens, and Bill of Middleton held the sinecure of Keeper of the Dour Fens.
t.Casinea: Nira, of Cantiarch's Hold, was Senator for Casinea.
t.Feroz: Chiara i Zayden i Riqueza was Senator for Feroz.
t.Hahnmark: Hengest Dun was Senator for Hahnmark.
t.Hercynia: Rhisiart Dancewalker was Senator for Hercynia.
t.Holberg: Irina Arkady Staryn Von Holberg was Senator for Holberg, and the Empress herself, Lisabetta Giacomi von Holberg, bore the territory's name.
t.Kahraman: Qusay i Kalamar i Guerra was Senator for Kahraman.
t.Kallavesa: Edythe Dunne was Senator for Kallavesa.
t.Karov: Pipski Bearonovitch Strascovich of the Vor'azi was Senator for Karov.
t.Madruga: Adan i Del-Toro i Riquezza was Senator for Madruga.
t.Miaren: Llewellyn Leafstalker was Senator for Miaren, and Tanwen Snowstep held the sinecure of Eternal Flame of Miaren.
t.Miekarova: Father Nikolovich Drakov was Senator for Miekarova.
t.Mitwold: William Guildenstern was Senator for Mitwold, Pride of the Marches.
t.Morrow: Ariadne of Auric Horizon was Senator for Morrow.
t.Mournwold: Robert Dunlain was Senator for Mournwold, the Mourn, and Mel Greenhill of Mourn was Conscience of the Senate.
t.Necropolis: Jeconiah, of Raven's Watch, was Senator for Necropolis.
t.Reikos: Cadeus, of the Shattered Tower, was Senator for Reikos, and the Great Forest at Reikos Bourse seat was held by Issachar for 200 Thrones.
t.Sarvos: Magdelena Alagna di Sarvos was Senator for Sarvos. Other titles held by people bearing the Sarvos name included Imperial Consul, Dean of the Academy, Archmage of Day and Mayor of Caricomare.
t.Segura: Avisena i Ezmara i Guerra was Senator for Segura.
t.Semmerholm: Lady Ailliena Devereux was Senator for Semmerholm.
t.Skarsind: Irontide Vio was Senator for Skarsind, and Irontide T'onk was Preceptor of the Skarsind College of Warcasting.
t.Tassato: Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato was Senator for Tassato, and Edwin Sanguineo di Tassato held the ministry of Steward of the Tassato Mana Exchange.
t.Temeschwar: The Senate seat for Temeschwar stood vacant this season.
t.Therunin: Cybi Farkas was Senator for Therunin.
t.Upwold: Henry Ward was Senator for Upwold, the Silver Chase.
t.Volodmartz: Alexei Volostra was Senator for Volodmartz.
t.Weirwater: Lady Eve Orzel was Senator for Weirwater, and the Weirwater Vales Bourse seat was held by Rada for 280 Thrones.

r.Holberg/Ennerlund: Mentioned in passing: the Great Pits of Ennerlund Bourse seat was held by Vasiliy Krenyenkov Valeskai Strascovich for 370 Thrones.

Authorise ambassador to Iron Confederacy.d: Proposed by the senator for Feroz and seconded by Upwold, the motion passed in Winter 381YE. It authorised the Imperial Ambassador to the Iron Confederacy to invite Duke Guiscard, identified on the page as the Duke of Kalino, to bring his troops into Feroz to deal with rebels from the Iron Confederacy there, on the understanding that they would withdraw immediately afterwards. The motion did not itself bring foreign troops into the Empire: the ambassador still needed to issue the invitation to the Duke for anything to happen.

n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast's senator for Feroz sought foreign help against Iron Confederacy rebels on Brass Coast soil, opening the way for Duke Guiscard's troops to enter one of the nation's territories.

t.Feroz: Feroz was named as the territory into which Duke Guiscard might be invited to send his forces to deal with the Iron Confederacy rebels before withdrawing, though the ambassador still had to issue the invitation.
t.Kalino: Kalino's Duke Guiscard was the ruler the ambassador was authorised to invite to send forces into Feroz against Iron Confederacy rebels.

Better world.d: At the Autumn Equinox 381YE Barbara Radz made it a crime in Rigia to kill or mistreat slaves, required them to be fed and watered, and told eastern princes to match her laws or leave her alliance, leaving her position precarious. The Synod was offered mandates urging Imperial captains to trade with Rigia rather than Vezak or Kavor, and the General Assembly passed one. Soon after, Soreana of Borașova, Tuernin of Limitu and other northern princes, after consulting Anton Trescher, supplied white seed through the Jarmish lodge in Tassato. It increases mana site yields for a season with steep diminishing returns, cannot be made in the Empire, and its price rose by about a fifth after the Winter 382YE sanctions on Jarm.

n.The League: League mana site owners gained the chance to buy white seed from the Jarmish merchants trading out of Tassato, and League alchemists such as Jaffo were among those examining the substance on behalf of figures like Prince Maria.

t.Tassato: The Jarmish lodge in Tassato, already known for its work with the Tassato Mana Exchange, became the sole point of sale for white seed in the Empire after a heavily armed Jarmish vessel delivered the first shipment shortly before the Winter Solstice.

Budded roses.d: The Druj had taken Axmure and destroyed the Gate, but four Dawnish generals united their armies and reconquered almost all of it. The Dawnish assembly sent Lady Caewyn of the Gryphon's Quill, with a song, to spur herb garden output for a year. Weirwater weavers and Queen Eleonaris gave gifts and favours to chosen champions at the Winter Solstice. The Senate commissioned the Harps of Astolat and accepted King Adamant's help to rebuild the Gate as the Adamant Gate. Sandro Visconti di Sarvos commissioned the Rose Towers at Lacuve by wayleave, with the Throne appointing their custodian. The Lady of the Semmerlak's Golden Causeway was completed before the Summer Solstice 382YE.

n.Dawn: Dawn's reconquest of Semmerholm stirred unprecedented national pride, and the nation gained a year-long boost to herb gardens, magical gifts for its champions, and several new great works and fortifications.
n.Druj: The Druj were routed from most of Semmerholm after their conquest of Axmure. They were defeated but not broken, and now face a rebuilt Gate and a hidden causeway that Dawnish armies could use to invade.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: the unliving horrors that threatened Weirwater are described as coming out of Varushka, and wise Varushkan allies helped free the Lady of the Semmerlak from her curse.

t.Astolat: Enchanters and weavers gathered at Weaving to plan great aeolian harps. The Senate commissioned the works, which were due shortly before the Spring Equinox 382YE and would share 45 extra crystal mana among Dawnish-owned mana sites.
t.Semmerholm: Dawn retook almost all of the territory from the Druj. The Senate accepted King Adamant's aid to rebuild the Gate, and the Rose Towers monument and the Golden Causeway were also commissioned here.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: the Barrens is named as the Druj's completed conquest from which they struck into Semmerholm, and as a land the Dawnish now expect to drive them from.
t.The Semmerlak: The Lady of the Semmerlak called young Pelleas of Lacre to her court and offered to raise a magical causeway across the lake for Dawnish armies alone. Its gate on the shore below Lacre was completed before the Summer Solstice 382YE.
t.Weirwater: Having seen the nobility defend them against the unliving, the weavers of Hawthorn, Applefel and Culwich crafted the Crown of Glorious Fire, the Belt of Knighthood and the Shield of the Seeker as year-long gifts for Dawnish champions.

r.Semmerholm/Axmure: Axmure had been conquered by the Druj, who destroyed the Gate there. It was swept up in the Dawnish counter-offensive that reconquered almost everything lost, and the Gate's rebuilding as the Adamant Gate has begun.
r.Semmerholm/Lacuve: Lacuve, home to Semmer's Rose and Lacre, is to see its minor defences turned into the Rose Towers, a place of pilgrimage commissioned by wayleave. The Golden Causeway lets Dawnish armies march from here across the Semmerlak.
r.The Barrens/Dawnguard: Mentioned in passing: the fall of Dawnguard is cited as a source of uncertainty among the yeomanry, and it is named as a land the Dawnish expect to drive the Druj from after Semmerholm.

Chain around my leg.d: At the Autumn Equinox a Day ritual devised by the Skywise and woven by Urizen's magicians, using the slave-made skull Defiance as its focus, was laid on general Mor'gur. While the Summer Storm resupplied, the Winter Sun spent the season in Casinea seeking their ancestors. They heard mostly enslaved orcs from Varushka, Temeschwar and Wintermark, including Skarsind, demanding freedom and vengeance on humans. A few older Thule and Jotun voices raged at their descendants. Affected orcs were haunted until the Winter Solstice, and Defiance became a mundane skull. Some soldiers swore oaths against slavery and wore hammer totems. Morg'ur's weirwood permanently changed the army's quality, granting the Break the chains order.

n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Highguard is not named, but the events took place in its territory of Casinea, where the orc armies rested.
n.Imperial Orcs: Both orc armies rested in Casinea, and the Winter Sun endured a harrowing revelation of their ancestors' slavery that haunted many soldiers and shaman until the Winter Solstice. The army was permanently transformed into Freedom Fighters able to launch the Break the chains order.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: some of the older, pre-slavery ancestors the orcs heard seemed to be Jotun, angry that their descendants serve unworthy humans.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: in the accompanying fiction, a Freeborn merchant selling herbs from Feroz was nearly attacked by a haunted orc.
n.The League: Many Winter Sun soldiers descend from slaves held in Temeschwar, so their shaman felt strong urges to flee or attack Temeschwari. The transformed army will be less comfortable alongside League armies, though discipline should prevent serious incidents.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: some of the oldest ancestral voices the orcs heard seemed to be Thule, raging at and disappointed in their descendants.
n.Urizen: Urizen's magicians wove the Day magic enchantment on general Mor'gur, the ritual behind the season's revelation.
n.Varushka: Most of the Winter Sun descend from orcs enslaved in Varushka, whose mines their ancestors worked. Shaman felt strong urges to flee from or attack Varushkans, and the army will remain uneasy alongside Varushkan forces.
n.Wintermark: Many of the ancestral voices were those of slaves held in Wintermark, which then included Skarsind. Shaman felt strong hostility towards Winterfolk, and the reformed army will be less comfortable fighting beside Wintermark's armies.

t.Casinea: Both Imperial Orc armies spent the season resting in Casinea, where the Winter Sun held drumming, meditation and fighting pits that brought on the revelation. Any orc who spent time there may have shared in the haunting.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: the fiction refers to herbs from the Spice Gardens of Feroz offered by a Freeborn merchant.
t.Skarsind: The revelation reminded the orcs that Skarsind's mines, in the homeland they now claim, were dug and worked by orc slaves when it was part of Wintermark, and many soldiers wept at the knowledge.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar was one of the places where the Winter Sun's ancestors lived and died as slaves, and orc shaman felt a powerful urge to flee from or attack Temeschwari.

Change to Imperial Breadbasket.d: Rowan Merrick, Keeper of the Imperial Breadbasket, announced that the Breadbasket would now be distributed to the Citadel Guard army rather than supporting the Mournwold, returning the commission to its role of contributing to the upkeep of Imperial armies. The change was approved by the Keeper and passed. It would take three months for the Breadbasket to begin supporting the Citadel Guard. At the same time, the money received by farms in the Marcher territories of Upwold, Mitwold and Bregasland was restored immediately.

n.The Marches: Marcher farms in Upwold, Mitwold and Bregasland had their Breadbasket income restored at once, while Breadbasket support for the Mournwold came to an end.

t.Bregasland: The money received by farms in Bregasland was restored immediately when the change passed.
t.Mitwold: Farms in Mitwold had the money they receive restored immediately as a result of the change.
t.Mournwold: The Imperial Breadbasket ceased to support the Mournwold, its resources being redirected to the Citadel Guard.
t.Upwold: The money received by farms in Upwold was restored immediately once the Breadbasket stopped supporting the Mournwold.

Charter Sarcombe market town.d: The motion awarded charter town status to Sarcombe, a Marcher town being rebuilt in the Mourn, so that if rebuilt it will be recognised as a market town across the Empire. The charter requires the townsfolk to form a council of aldermen that elects a Mayoress annually. She speaks for the town to the Senator for the Mourn, who agrees to give her a fair hearing. The council controls the town budget and appoints a Town Clerk who reports to the Imperial Civil Service. Sarcombe may hold a monthly market and run a permanent trading post for mined goods, both funded by levies. It must also host an outpost of the Imperial Militia.

n.The Marches: The Marcher town of Sarcombe gains Imperial recognition as a market town once rebuilt, with its own elected council and Mayoress, and the right to profit from its people's mining expertise through a trading post.

t.Mournwold: Sarcombe, a town being rebuilt in the Mournwold, is chartered to hold a monthly market and a mined-goods trading post and to host a Militia outpost, with its Mayoress keeping the Mourn's senator informed.

Construct Arsenal in Sarvos.d: The motion, proposed by the senator for Sarvos and seconded by the senator for Kahraman, sought Senate approval to build a Great Work in Sarvos. It was believed to relate to the opportunity to build the Sarvos Dockyard and Arsenal. The proposed construction would have enriched the port fleets by 900 rings, shared equally among them, and would have given the League the possibility of raising a Navy in future. The work was to be self-funded rather than paid for from the Imperial treasury. The Senate did not pass the motion, so the arsenal was not commissioned that season.

n.The League: The League lost, for now, a self-funded route to enriching its port fleets and to the possibility of raising a League Navy, after a motion backed by its own senators for Sarvos and Kahraman failed.

t.Sarvos: The proposed dockyard and arsenal in Sarvos was not approved, so the territory's ports did not gain the Great Work or the promised enrichment of its fleets.

Construct Gate in Semmerholm.d: Proposed by the senator for Semmerholm and seconded by Holberg, the commission drew on an opportunity offered by the Eternal Adamant. It required 160 wains of white granite but no labour, would take twelve months, and carried an upkeep of 18 thrones. It did not count against the Senate's limit on commissions. The granite came largely from Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar over several seasons, with further contributions from the Silent Sentinel opportunity and a bequest from Ailliena Devereux. The final wains were supplied by over-enthusiastic koboldi, whom Adamant scolded for profligacy. The finished fortification would have 6000 effective strength. The work could falter if the Conclave declared enmity against Adamant.

n.Dawn: Dawn gained the restored Gate in Semmerholm as an Unbreakable fortification worth 6000 effective strength. Its senator proposed the work and Holberg seconded it, adding to the defences of Dawnish lands.

t.Semmerholm: The Gate was rebuilt in Semmerholm with the Eternal Adamant's aid, using 160 wains of white granite and leaving the territory with a 6000-strength Unbreakable fortification.

Construct Harps of Astolat.d: The motion took advantage of an existing opportunity to raise a powerful great work in Astolat. Besides the 150 thrones, it required 35 wains of weirwood, 15 wains of mithril and 100 crowns, and took three months to complete. Bohemond De Rondell supplied all of the materials and crowns after the Winter Solstice 381YE. The finished great work means every mana site in Astolat owned by a Dawnish citizen shares an additional 45 crystal mana each season, provided the central harp at Weaving remains unmolested.

n.Dawn: Dawnish citizens who own mana sites in Astolat gain a share of 45 extra crystal mana each season, a project funded through the materials and crowns supplied by Bohemond De Rondell.

t.Astolat: The Harps of Astolat were built here, and every Dawnish-owned mana site in the territory now benefits from them so long as the central harp at Weaving stays unmolested.

Construct Lorenzo's Legacy of Prosperity.d: Proposed by the senator for Reikos and seconded by the senator for Casinea, the motion commissioned a great work costing 40 wains of mithril and 10 Thrones, taking three months to complete. It was to be funded by Lorenzo 'La Volpe' and the Bloody Butchers Guild of Temeschwar, and was centred near Long Tom's Brewery in Anvil, honouring Long Tom Goodfellow, Exemplar of Prosperity, as inspiration for the Butchers Benevolence and pilgrimage along the Blood Red Roads. Lorenzo 'La Volpe' Macelliao von Temeschwar provided the full cost after the Winter Solstice. The completed work provides 37 crystal mana each season, shared amongst Casinean citizens who own mana sites.

n.Highguard: Highguard gained a great work in its territory of Casinea that adds 37 crystal mana each season for its citizens there who own mana sites, with the motion proposed by Reikos and seconded by Casinea.
n.The League: A League patron, Lorenzo 'La Volpe' Macelliao von Temeschwar, together with the Bloody Butchers Guild of Temeschwar, funded the great work in full and gave it his name.

t.Casinea: The great work was built in Casinea near Long Tom's Brewery in Anvil, yielding 37 crystal mana each season shared amongst Casinean mana site owners.
t.Temeschwar: The Bloody Butchers Guild of Temeschwar and Lorenzo 'La Volpe' von Temeschwar were named as the great work's funders, extending Temeschwar's influence through the Butchers Benevolence and the Blood Red Roads.

Construct Lorenzo's Legacy of Vigilance.d: Proposed by the senator for Sermersuaq and seconded by Hahnmark, the motion commissioned a great work in New Dunhall at a cost of 40 wains of mithril and 10 thrones, taking three months to complete. It was to be built by the Asavean Architect, with the commission overseen by Almodin Oktístis, Priest of the Builder. After the Winter Solstice 381YE, Lorenzo 'La Volpe' Macelliao von Temeschwar provided the full mithril and thrones. Once complete, the great work provides 37 crystal mana each season, shared among those citizens of Hahnmark who own a mana site.

n.The League: A League citizen, Lorenzo 'La Volpe' Macelliao von Temeschwar, together with the Bloody Butchers Guild, bankrolled the entire great work, which bears his name.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark gains a great work in its territory of Hahnmark that delivers 37 crystal mana each season to Hahnmark's mana site owners, with Wintermark's senators for Sermersuaq and Hahnmark proposing and seconding the motion.

t.Hahnmark: The great work is built in New Dunhall and provides 37 crystal mana each season, spread among citizens who own mana sites in Hahnmark.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: the funders, Lorenzo 'La Volpe' von Temeschwar and the Bloody Butchers Guild, are identified as being of Temeschwar.

Construct Rose Towers.d: Announced under a Wayleave, the Rose Towers would create the Imperial title The Queen's Rose, with custodianship of a place of pilgrimage that provides 12 doses of liao and 24 votes in the Imperial Synod. Although the wayleave referred to Semmer's Rose, the work actually uses the minor fortifications at Lacre in Lacuve, replacing the minor benefits they provided. It cost 15 wains of white granite and 30 crowns and takes three months to complete. Sandro Visconti di Sarvos supplied the materials after the Spring Equinox 382YE. Unusually, the title is appointed annually by the Throne as Monarch of Dawn, supported by Dawnish national assembly statements; without a Throne it cannot be appointed.

n.Dawn: Dawn gains a pilgrimage sinecure, The Queen's Rose, in its own lands, and its national assembly's recognition of the Empress as Queen of Dawn secured the Throne's right to appoint the title.

t.Semmerholm: Semmerholm is the site of the Rose Towers, a new place of pilgrimage yielding liao and Synod votes, built in place of existing minor fortification benefits.

r.Semmerholm/Lacuve: The minor fortifications at Lacre in Lacuve are converted into the Rose Towers, replacing their previous minor benefits with a place of pilgrimage.

Construct Sarvos Mana Exchange.d: The motion sought to exploit the opportunity created by the Tassato Mana Ministry by building a second ministry in Sarvos to oversee the purchase and sale of crystal mana. It passed, at a cost of 12 mithril and 24 crowns and three months' construction. After the Winter Solstice 381YE Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar provided the 12 wains of mithril and the 24 crowns. On completion the project will create the Sarvos Mana Exchange ministry and a new Imperial title, the Steward of the Sarvos Mana Exchange, to oversee it, with the position appointed by the League.

n.The League: The League gains a second mana ministry and a new national title, the Steward of the Sarvos Mana Exchange, strengthening its hold on the Empire's crystal mana trade.

t.Sarvos: Sarvos is to host the new Sarvos Mana Exchange, a ministry overseeing the purchase and sale of crystal mana, due to take three months to build.
t.Tassato: Tassato's senator proposed the motion, which builds on the opportunity created by the existing Tassato Mana Ministry.

Construct Seren's Whispering Garden.d: Proposed by the senator for Miaren and seconded by Therunin, the motion sought to exploit the opportunity presented by the Eye of Serenael. Construction would have needed 35 wains of white granite, 35 wains of weirwood and 17 Thrones and 4 Crowns, and taken six months. Once complete, the great work would have safely channelled the magic of the Eye, and possibly several smaller regio, throughout Miaren. Every herb garden would have shared a seasonal bounty of 36 crystal mana and every mana site a bounty of 54 random herbs. The motion passed in principle, but the commission lapsed at the Autumn Equinox 382YE without being completed.

n.Navarr: Navarr's senator for Miaren proposed the great work, which would have enriched the nation's herb gardens and mana sites in Miaren, but the commission lapsed unbuilt.

t.Miaren: Miaren was to host the great work, which would have channelled the Eye of Serenael's magic throughout the territory, but the commission lapsed in Autumn 382YE.

r.Miaren/Serenael: The Eye of Serenael was the source of magic the garden was meant to harness and spread through Miaren, but because the commission lapsed, that power went untapped.

Construct Temeschwar Mana Exchange.d: Proposed by the senator for Temeschwar and seconded by Miaren, the motion sought to build a mana exchange ministry in Temeschwar, self-funded and described as part of an opportunity offered by the Jarmish. It cost 12 wains of mithril and 24 crowns and would take three months to complete. Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar provided the full cost after the Winter Solstice. The outcome is a mana exchange ministry and a new Imperial title, the Magic Butcher, to oversee it. The Constitutional Court noted that the construction was not tied to any Jarmish offer, but arose from the completion of the great works known as Lorenzo's Legacies of Virtue in the League.

n.The League: The League gains a ministry for trading crystal mana and a new Imperial title, the Magic Butcher, whose holder is appointed by the League's senators, funded by the League citizen Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar.

t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar is to host the new mana exchange ministry, paid for with 12 wains of mithril and 24 crowns from Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar and taking three months to complete.

Construct place of pilgrimage in Casinea.d: Proposed by the senator for Necropolis and seconded by Weirwater, the motion commissioned a grand tower as a place of pilgrimage at the Sentinel in Casinea. It was self-funded, costing 25 wains of white granite and 50 crowns, with three months to complete. Rhesa provided the materials and money after the Winter Solstice 381YE. Construction could only begin once the Silent Sentinel had received a True Liao consecration. On completion it creates a sinecure overseen by the Castellan of the Silent Sentinel, who is also custodian of the fortress. The Highborn National Assembly appoints the title.

n.Highguard: Highborn senators proposed and seconded the motion, and Rhesa funded it. The Highborn National Assembly gains the right to appoint the Castellan of the Silent Sentinel, custodian of the fortress and its pilgrimage tower.

t.Casinea: A grand tower of pilgrimage was to rise at the Silent Sentinel in Casinea once the site had received a True Liao consecration, with a new Castellan overseeing both the sinecure and the fortress.

Construct spy network in the Mountains o.d: The commission needed 10 wains of weirwood, three months' work and upkeep of 2 thrones a season. Nira of Cantiarch's Hold supplied the weirwood and 20 crowns of labour after the Winter Solstice 381YE. Work could only begin once the Empire controlled a region bordering the territory: Lustri, Occursion, Ossuary or Apstrus. The Grendel and Druj occupation of Zenith and Spiral stalled progress. The conquest of Ossuary in Spiral restored access, and the network was completed shortly before the Summer Solstice 382YE. After Summer 382YE a significant force of scouts supported it and uncovered extensive details of the Mountains of the Moon and some information about the Tsark folk living there.

n.Druj: The Druj occupation of Zenith, along with the occupation of Spiral, cut the Empire off from the Mountains of the Moon and halted work after the Winter Solstice 381YE.
n.Grendel: Grendel's hold on Spiral, along with the occupation of Zenith, blocked work on the network until the Empire conquered Ossuary and regained access.
n.Urizen: The network was aimed at the lands beyond Zenith, but with Zenith occupied, Urizen's border regions could not serve as the route in.

t.Mountains of the Moon: An Imperial spy network was completed here before Summer 382YE, and scouts then uncovered extensive details of the territory and some information about its Tsark inhabitants.
t.Spiral: Occupation of Spiral initially blocked the commission, but the conquest of Ossuary there gave the Empire the access it needed to finish the work.
t.Zenith: Zenith borders the Mountains of the Moon, but its occupation by the Druj helped stall the commission after Winter 381YE.

r.Spiral/Apstrus: Mentioned in passing: listed as one of the regions bordering the Mountains of the Moon whose control would allow work to begin.
r.Spiral/Ossuary: The Empire's conquest of Ossuary restored access to the Mountains of the Moon and allowed the spy network to be finished before the Summer Solstice 382YE.
r.Zenith/Lustri: Mentioned in passing: listed as one of the regions bordering the Mountains of the Moon whose control would allow work to begin.
r.Zenith/Occursion: Mentioned in passing: listed as one of the regions bordering the Mountains of the Moon whose control would allow work to begin.

Construct walls of Holberg.d: The motion called for raising Holberg's walls from their current level to twice their effectiveness and requested funds to begin building. The listed costs were 200 wains of white granite, 50 thrones and a year of construction, with the upkeep of the walls rising to 28 thrones each season. After the Spring Equinox 382YE, Irina Kardaovich, Caerwyn Von Holberg of The Feasting Crow and Imperatrix Lisabetta von Holberg all donated granite, and the Silent Sentinel opportunity supplied more. Lisabetta completed the supply with 72 wains after the Summer Solstice. The finished walls gave Holberg city an effective defensive military strength of 12,000.

n.The League: The League's senators drove the project, and League citizens largely supplied the granite, including donations from Imperatrix Lisabetta von Holberg and The Feasting Crow. The result greatly strengthened the defences of one of its great cities.

t.Holberg: Holberg city's walls were greatly improved, reaching an effective defensive strength of 12,000, but their upkeep rose to 28 thrones each season.

Declare Mournwold thralls foreigners.d: Proposed by the senator for Upwold and seconded by the senator for Segura, the motion settled the legal status of the former Jotun thralls who remained in the Mournwold. It passed, and the orc thralls there became foreigners in the eyes of the Empire. As a consequence it became legal to trade with them, while it became illegal to force them off their land, kill them, engage them with Imperial armies or steal their holdings.

n.The Marches: Marcher settlers in the Mournwold must now live alongside the former Jotun thralls as lawful foreigners, free to trade with them but barred from driving them off, killing them or taking their holdings, and the motion was proposed by Upwold's senator.

t.Mournwold: The orc thralls left in the Mournwold gained legal protection as foreigners, so trading with them became lawful while evicting, killing or robbing them, or sending Imperial armies against them, became illegal.

Decommission Verthandi spy network.d: Proposed by the senator for Kallavesi and seconded by Karsk, the motion text calls for decommissioning the Otkodov spy network, while the summary describes it as the Verthandi spy network in Otkodov. It passed at a cost of 5 Thrones, taken directly from the treasury, and takes three months to complete. The network's 2-Throne upkeep was still paid for that season. As a result, the spy network in Verthandi will be rolled up discreetly, and military units can no longer be assigned to it.

n.Thule: The Empire is dismantling its covert network in lands held by Thule, so the Thule-held territories it covered will no longer be watched by it, and Imperial armies can no longer be assigned to it.

t.Otkodov: The motion text names the network as the Otkodov spy network, and the summary places the Verthandi network in Otkodov. Its decommissioning ends that Imperial espionage presence there.
t.Verthandi: The Imperial spy network in Verthandi, a territory held by Thule, will be rolled up discreetly over three months, and military units can no longer be assigned to it.

Dusty old dust.d: After the Winter Solstice, Imperial congregations would again sell liao for 18 rings a dose, as the Nemorian temple pushed up Axou demand. The Sumaah sent negotiators to Anvil to meet Ambassador Vera Runova Helgrod, though Zemeh stayed closed. Fleets trading with Nemoria gained extra gloaming and orichalcum, despite Sumaah-inspired unrest among the satrapies. Jarm's Vezak offered extra crystal mana. The Upwold enclave and the Blood Red Roads drew more Faraden merchants, who hoped for enclaves in Karov and Astolat. A heretical pamphlet spread interest in their faith. Axos took note of heavy Imperial trade. Sarcophan dealings with the Grendel caused friction, and the Senate paid 50 Thrones to open Robec.

n.Dawn: Faraden merchants hoped for an enclave in Astolat to reach Dawnish luxuries and wine, and Suranni soldiers of Duke Guiscard fought alongside Dawn's knights and war-witches in their triumphant Semmerholm campaign, though they openly disdained Dawnish magic.
n.Grendel: The Grendel were believed to have noted the many merchant ships sailing east from the Bay of Catazar to Axos. Their agreement with the Sarcophan Delves and reports of pirates selling plundered Imperial goods to Sarcophan merchants stirred resentment.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: Sarcophan traders were said to travel as far north as Skarsind.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Faraden mithril offered at the public auction was transported through Jotun lands at some expense.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn national assembly could appoint a Liaison to the completed Temple of the Way in Nemoria. The planned road links through Anduz promised prosperity to Segura and Madruga, while Freeborn mariners were angered by Grendel pirates selling stolen goods to the Sarcophan.
n.The League: A heretical pamphlet by Romero di Sarvos surfaced in Tassato, where a Faraden mercenary hall was mooted. Faraden carts reached Temeschwar and Holberg, and Sarvosan mariners were incensed at Grendel plunder sold to the Sarcophan.
n.The Marches: The completed Faraden enclave in Upwold brought prosperity, and Faraden merchants were eager to buy Marcher food and drink, especially beer, apples and grain.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Sarcophan representatives at Torfast Trading Post were eager to meet merchants travelling the new roads south from Otkodov.
n.Varushka: Vera Runova Helgrod of Varushka, as Ambassador, was expected to meet the Sumaah negotiators at Anvil. The Faraden hoped for an enclave in Karov to gain access to Varushkan wood and green iron.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Faraden carts visited Kalpaheim, and Sarcophan traders travelled as far north as Hahnmark.

t.Astolat: Faraden merchants openly hoped to see a trading enclave established in Astolat, giving them access to Dawnish luxuries.
t.Bay of Catazar: Large numbers of Imperial merchant vessels sailed east from the Bay towards Axos. Sarcophan ships, protected by their agreement with the Grendel, were regular visitors to its ports, which caused friction in waterside taverns.
t.Feroz: Revolutionaries in southern Feroz targeting Suranni merchants caused a sharp drop in trade with the Iron Confederacy. The Senate disbursed 50 Thrones to the Senator for Feroz to open the port of Robec to Imperial captains.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: Sarcophan traders were said to travel inland as far north as Hahnmark.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: a few adventurous Faraden traders made it as far as Holberg.
t.Kalino: Mentioned in passing: Duke Guiscard was named as the new ruler of Kalino, and his soldiers fought alongside Dawn in Semmerholm.
t.Karov: Faraden merchants hoped to see a trading enclave in Karov, which would give them access to Varushkan wood.
t.Madruga: A completed road link between Anduz and Tassato was expected to bring significant prosperity to the Freeborn merchants of Madruga, though work had not yet begun.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: merchants travelling the new roads south from Otkodov were sought out by Sarcophan traders at Torfast Trading Post.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: the heretical pamphlet's author was Romero di Sarvos, and Sarvosan mariners were angered by Grendel plunder being sold to the Sarcophan.
t.Segura: A Senate commission was underway to extend the Blood Red Roads to Anduz in Segura, promising prosperity for its merchants. Suranni traders occasionally came north through Segura.
t.Semmerholm: Dawn waged a triumphant campaign in Semmerholm, aided by Iron Confederacy soldiers of Duke Guiscard who disdained the magic and liao-using priests they saw there.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: Sarcophan traders were said to travel inland as far north as Skarsind.
t.Tassato: A heretical pamphlet on the Faraden faith surfaced in Tassato and spread along the Blood Red Roads. Tassato was also a proposed site for a Faraden mercenary hall and for a future road link to Anduz.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: brightly painted Faraden ox-carts were visiting Temeschwar.
t.Upwold: The first official Faraden trading enclave was completed in Upwold, bringing prosperity to the territory as Faraden merchants bought Marcher food and drink.
t.Volodmartz: Mentioned in passing: Sarcophan traders were said to travel inland as far north as Volodmartz.

Fly high.d: Holmauer, ruined during the Druj occupation, was transformed into a grand park with orchards, a bathhouse, an open-air venue and the Imperial Menagerie. Merchant-princes proposed turning Holfried into a garden city (60 wains of weirwood, 40 of white granite, 25 Thrones), with a University alternative producing healing herbs. The menagerie could be expanded for 20 weirwood and 5 Thrones. Monoliths boosted League-owned mana sites, allowing either expansion of the Tassato Mana Exchange or new exchanges in the other cities. Meanwhile Bite, a blue powder heightening confidence and aggression, spread from Holberg, fuelling bravo brawls. The Senate declined the garden city but commissioned the Temeschwar and Sarvos Mana Exchanges; the menagerie opportunity remains open.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the Dawnish are said to have severely bloodied the Druj's noses in Semmerholm.
n.Druj: The Druj have left Holberg and show no sign of returning, their attention now turned to Dawn and Urizen, where they have reportedly suffered heavily in Semmerholm.
n.The League: The League's cities flourished with three completed great works and new mana exchanges in Temeschwar and Sarvos, though the Senate passed on the Holberg garden city and the narcotic Bite spread among its bravos.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Urizen is named alongside Dawn as where Druj attention now seems focused.

t.Holberg: Holberg completed its Grand Park and was offered a garden city transformation, which the Senate declined, while Bite originated here and bravo brawls increased.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos gained a Mana Exchange commissioned by the Senate, while Bite began to appear and brawls rose to a lesser degree.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: the Dawnish are reported to have badly bloodied the Druj in Semmerholm.
t.Tassato: The Tassato Mana Exchange could have been dramatically expanded, though the Senate instead built exchanges elsewhere, and Bite-fuelled brawls between bravos increased here.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar gained a Mana Exchange commissioned by the Senate, benefiting from Lorenzo's monolith, while Bite began to appear on its streets.

r.Holberg/Holfried: Merchant-princes proposed turning war-scarred Holfried into a garden city or a source of healing herbs, but the Senate declined and the opportunity expired.
r.Holberg/Holmauer: Holmauer's ruined suburbs were transformed into the Grand Park with the Imperial Menagerie, whose expansion with exotic beasts remains open for the Senate to commission.

Foggy mountain top.d: House Vexille's shroud lifted, but a strengthened magnitude-fifty Night shroud persisted over Semmerholm and the Barrens, making naga there unusually secretive. Distil the Serpent's Stone kept producing shadow eggs. Aleksandra's Watch in Karsk was finished early with Autumn magic, and a serpent-garrisoned castle briefly rose in the Morass. Richard of Holberg offered designs for menhirs in Mournwold, a loom on Starstep in Morrow (later lost in 385YE) and a garden in Tassato. Eleonaris became patron of the Icy Crag, Jaheris sought his champions, Sadogua sought a lost medallion, Donum hunted orc-enslavement relics, hare-marked briars aided Zenith and Mournwold, and the Senate's treasure ship was sunk for Rhianos.

n.Dawn: House Vexille's star-shroud lifted across most of the Empire but persisted, strengthened, over Dawnish Semmerholm, where the koboldi hope to rebuild the Gate and Eleonaris's attention is fixed on Dawn.
n.Druj: The shroud hiding the stars remained over the Druj-held Barrens, while the castle that rose in the Morass resembled a mirror-image of the old Druj fortress at Rebeshof.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Richard of Holberg is described as having been rescued from the Grendel by Imperial heroes the previous Summer.
n.Imperial Orcs: The sinister herald Donum was seen in Skarsind questioning antiquity collectors, miners and historians, seeking relics of orc enslavement in exchange for old coins, heart's blood and minor boons.
n.Jotun: The stars, hidden for a year over Jotun-held Liathaven, returned to its night skies along with the rest of the Empire.
n.The League: A Night-born castle garrisoned by serpent heralds friendly only to League citizens briefly rose in Holberg, Richard of Holberg offered a garden design for Tassato, Donum prowled Temeschwar, and a Madrugan senator paid for the ship sacrificed to Rhianos.
n.The Marches: Richard of Holberg designed a network of menhirs for Mournwold offering crystal mana and protection from curses, and hare-marked briars came to aid struggling Mournwold farmers and refugees.
n.Thule: Thule orcs in Krevsaty reportedly took considerable interest in the Autumn magic used to complete Aleksandra's Watch early.
n.Urizen: Urizen lost the Halls of Knowledge from Zenith only for the college to reappear, empty, in Peregro in Morrow, and was offered a design for a starlight loom on Starstep in Operus.
n.Varushka: Aleksandra's Watch in Karsk was completed early, Eleonaris became patron of the Icy Crag in Miekarova, Donum roamed Varushka seeking orc-enslavement relics, and Sadogua's heralds hinted his lost medallion went to the Gremani family.

t.Bay of Catazar: The Senate's treasure ship Adventure was sailed into the bay and scuttled, and Rhianos consumed it in a storm.
t.Holberg: A dripping castle of mud, black stone and solid mist, garrisoned by spear-wielding serpent heralds, rose in the Morass after the Autumn Equinox and sank again before the Winter Solstice.
t.Karsk: The Senate-commissioned fortification Aleksandra's Watch was completed several months ahead of schedule through powerful Autumn magic.
t.Liathaven: The stars, absent for a year over Liathaven, were fully restored to its skies by the week before the summit.
t.Miekarova: Eleonaris, the Lion of Summer, became patron of the Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun, and is likely to send someone to meet its Master of Ice and Darkness.
t.Morrow: The Halls of Knowledge reappeared in Peregro, and Richard of Holberg designed a loom on Starstep in Operus to spin starlight into prismatic ink for a Weaver of Stars.
t.Mournwold: Richard of Holberg proposed menhirs across the territory providing crystal mana and protection from curses, while hare-marked briars offered food, labour and healing to the needy.
t.Semmerholm: A strengthened Night shroud of magnitude fifty kept the stars hidden and blocked lesser scrying, naga spending time there grew intensely secretive, and the koboldi hoped to rebuild its Gate.
t.Skarsind: The herald Donum was seen talking to collectors, quarry workers and historians in Skarsind, seeking relics of orc enslavement.
t.Tassato: Richard of Holberg designed a night-flowering garden at a ruined weirwood tower in Madeiras, creating a Watcher of the Wheel who would harvest magical materials each season if built.
t.Temeschwar: The herald Donum was seen in Temeschwar seeking relics related to orc enslavement from antiquarians and workers.
t.The Barrens: The shroud hiding the stars persisted over the Barrens, impeding scrying, and naga who spent time there became markedly secretive.
t.Zenith: The Halls of Knowledge vanished into shimmering mist, leaving a shallow mountain lake and some scholars unaccounted for, while hare-marked briars aided Zenith's needy.

r.Holberg/Rebeshof: Mentioned in passing: witnesses realised the Morass castle looked like a mirror-image of the Druj castle that once stood at Rebeshof.
r.Holberg/The Morass: An enchanted fortress of mud and mist, guarded by serpent heralds hostile to all but League citizens, rose here and sank back before the Solstice.
r.Karsk/Krevsaty: Thule orcs in Krevsaty showed considerable interest in the magic used to finish Aleksandra's Watch.
r.Karsk/Lestasny: Mentioned in passing: reports from Lestasny describe the interest shown in the magic used to build Aleksandra's Watch.
r.Morrow/Operus: Richard of Holberg proposed a grand loom atop the Day-aligned regio on Starstep, a design later lost after the 385YE Cold Sun attacks.
r.Morrow/Peregro: The Halls of Knowledge materialised intact but lifeless beside one of Peregro's largest hot springs.
r.Tassato/Madeiras: A ruined, ivy-covered tower with a weirwood tree in northern Madeiras was proposed as the site of Richard of Holberg's Watcher of the Wheel garden.

Froggy went a'courting.d: The Thule treaty of Summer 379YE expires at the Summer Solstice 382YE. It had brought an embassy in Miekarova, the Gift of the Dwindling Star, returned slaves and the Blood Cloak, and crystal mana trade through Crow's Ridge. The Thule built a slave-made castle in Krevsaty and showed armies there and on the Silver Peaks, without hostility. Their ambassador met Yevgeni Katzev, but no new treaty was reached. A Grendel delegation landed at Sarvos under truce, and its treaty offer was deemed unacceptable. The Great Forest orcs in Therunin sought clarity on ritual texts and payment. Cybi Farkas's ten wains of weirwood let work begin on the Holt of the Oak, though much remains outstanding.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are named as the reason the Great Forest orcs were forced to flee their homes.
n.Grendel: Speaker Morna's Grendel delegation sailed into Sarvos under a flag of truce to speak with the Imperial Consul at Anvil, but the peace treaty they offered was deemed unacceptable.
n.Imperial Orcs: Slaves taken from Skarsind had been returned under the Thule peace, and Imperial merchants travelled north from Skarsind to trade directly with the Thule while Thule traders passed through Crow's Ridge.
n.Navarr: Therunin's people were urged to share herbs with the Great Forest orcs, the Thimble's Navarr custodian lost 4 wains of weirwood a season, and Therunin's senator Cybi Farkas supplied the weirwood that let work on the Holt of the Oak begin. There were also rumours of Navarr dealings with the Thule over the vallorn.
n.The League: The League city of Sarvos received the Grendel ship bound for Anvil and gave it a frosty welcome, while its magistrates reminded everyone that the Grendel were protected by Imperial law.
n.Thule: With their three-year treaty ending in Summer 382YE, the Thule sent an ambassador to Anvil and showed restrained strength with armies in Krevsaty and the Silver Peaks. No new treaty was agreed.
n.Varushka: Varushka had gained an embassy in Miekarova and the Gift of the Dwindling Star under the Thule peace, but now faced a new Thule castle and army in Krevsaty, which was reported by the people of Branoc and Crowslook.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark had recovered slaves and the Blood Cloak from the Thule, with a dozen more slaves returned to Raknar, but it remained bitter over the ceding of the Silver Peaks, where Suaq hunters now saw large numbers of orcs.

t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: rumours spoke of contact between the Thule and the Navarr of Hercynia, including talk of agreements on the secrets of the vallorn.
t.Karsk: The Thule built a slave-made castle in the Krevsaty region of Karsk and stationed what was almost certainly an army there, though it showed no signs of hostility.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: rumours spoke of contact between the Thule and the Navarr of Miaren, including talk of agreements on the secrets of the vallorn.
t.Miekarova: Mentioned in passing: an Imperial embassy to the Thule had been built in Miekarova under the peace treaty.
t.Otkodov: The dragons of Otkodov sent a delegation to Anvil to discuss the expiring treaty, while a few Imperial merchants traded directly with the Thule in southern Otkodov.
t.Sarvos: An Asavean-style Grendel ship docked at Sarvos under a flag of truce on its way to Anvil, and received a frosty reception given the Grendel's last visit.
t.Sermersuaq: Suaq hunters saw large numbers of orcs moving on the flanks of the Thule-held Silver Peaks, where bitterness over the ceding of that region persisted.
t.Skarsind: Slaves taken from Skarsind had been returned by the Thule, Thule merchants passed through Crow's Ridge, and a few Imperial merchants travelled north from Skarsind to trade in Otkodov.
t.Therunin: The Great Forest orcs living in Therunin received herbs, a share of the Thimble's weirwood and ritual texts, and work on their weirwood fortification, the Holt of the Oak, began after Cybi Farkas supplied ten wains.

r.Karsk/Branoc: Residents of Branoc reported the new Thule castle and army in neighbouring Krevsaty.
r.Karsk/Crowslook: Residents of Crowslook reported the new Thule castle and army in neighbouring Krevsaty.
r.Karsk/Krevsaty: The Thule built a castle in Krevsaty using slave labour and stationed a substantial force there, which appeared to be drilling and hunting rather than preparing to attack.
r.Sermersuaq/East Floes: Suaq hunters in East Floes reported large numbers of orcs moving on the flanks of the Silver Peaks.
r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: The Thule-held Silver Peaks, home to a castle conjured from the Summer realm, saw large numbers of orcs on its flanks, while Wintermark remained bitter over its ceding.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount: Suaq hunters in Suaq Fount reported large numbers of orcs moving on the flanks of the Silver Peaks.
r.Skarsind/Crow’s Ridge: Thule merchants travelled through Crow's Ridge as part of the Senate-approved Northern trade network, bringing crystal mana to Imperial traders.

Hard times.d: The rebels, the same faction that sought the Synod's aid a year earlier, camped near Feroz's southern border. From there they raided Kalino, robbing Suranni caravans, sabotaging mines and farms and freeing slaves, while buying supplies from Freeborn traders. Duke Guiscard's envoy said he would not cross the border without explicit Imperial permission. He offered future sales of white granite from Arav's Delve if the problem was resolved. The options set out were to declare the rebels barbarians, eject them with an Imperial army, invite the Duke in, ignore them, or aid them. Freeborn visitors reported an unknown consecration aura and Imperial liao in the camp. A hallowed item was sent to the Imperial Inquisitor for examination.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Zadkiel de Coeurdefer of Dawn, the Ambassador to the Iron Confederacy, was briefed by the civil service, and it was the Ambassador whom the Senate authorised to invite the Duke's forces in.
