n.The Brass Coast: The rebels set up camp in Freeborn Feroz and traded with Freeborn merchants. The hakima Marcela i Erigo obtained a hallowed item from the camp and sent it to Anvil, raising concerns about the priests preaching there.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the page gives no specific role to the Bay of Catazar.
t.Feroz: About two hundred rebels made makeshift camps near Feroz's southern border and raided Kalino from there. The Senate's decision opened the way for Suranni troops to enter Feroz to suppress them.
t.Kalino: Duke Guiscard's Kalino suffered cross-border raids on caravans, mines and farms, with dozens of Suranni killed and slaves freed. The Duke offered future white granite sales from Arav's Delve in return for help.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: the in-character story describes Marcela's chicken as the plumpest to be found in Segura.

House of earth.d: After the Jotun retreat, large numbers of unarmed, unwarlike thralls remained, mainly in Green March, Southmoor and Chalkdowns. Fed by 75 thrones a season of Imperial aid since Summer, they had returned to their farms and could now feed themselves. The page set out the options: declare peace and treat them as foreigners, convert them to the Way with 50 doses of liao, or evict them by military force. Eviction would have freed land for an extra Marcher army and let the Military Council claim the Golden Hoof, Black Hill and Eversweet Orchard as spoils, but would have angered many Mournwolders. In the end the Marcher Assembly sent Sister Meredith to preach, and the Senate recognised the thralls as foreigners, making eviction illegal.

n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orc Assembly had resolved to send missionaries led by Bloodcrow Losak, and could pass a similar mandate to preach to the thralls. It remained unclear whether converted thralls could ever become Imperial Orcs, given orc scepticism and that they live in the Mournwold rather than Skarsind.
n.Jotun: Thralls left behind by the retreating Jotun armies now live under Imperial rule and were recognised as foreigners protected by Imperial law. Across the border, Ysra and Gudmundur were said to have fallen out over the thrall deaths, with Gudmundur reportedly swearing a blood oath of vengeance.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: any thralls driven west through Liathaven might have faced attack from the Navarr or the vallorn on the way.
n.The Marches: Mournwold Marchers had been quietly trading with the thralls, who hold the best farmland and so prevented the Marches raising an extra army from the Mourn. The Marcher Assembly sent Sister Meredith to convert them, and the Marcher egregore insisted the thralls could never become Marchers.

t.Hordalant: Mentioned in passing: thralls evicted from the Mournwold, or stripped of their property, would most likely have gone back over the border to Hordalant.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: any thralls driven out of the Mournwold would have faced a dangerous trek west through Liathaven.
t.Mournwold: Thralls hold about three fifths of the territory, including the Golden Hoof, Black Hill and Eversweet Orchard. With the Senate recognising them as foreigners, they cannot legally be driven from their farms or homes, and they will pay taxes but will not support Imperial armies.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: raised as a complication if converted Mournwold thralls were ever to become Imperial Orcs while living in the Mournwold rather than Skarsind.

r.Mournwold/Alderly: Mentioned in passing: the Feni-infested woods at Alderly are described as largely a no-man's land, held by neither Marchers nor thralls.
r.Mournwold/Chalkdowns: Chalkdowns is one of the regions with especially large numbers of Jotun thralls, who now farm there under Imperial protection as recognised foreigners.
r.Mournwold/Green March: Green March holds a particularly large thrall population working its farms, and they can no longer legally be evicted following the Senate's recognition.
r.Mournwold/Southmoor: Southmoor is home to many of the remaining thralls, who have returned to their farms and are now protected from eviction as foreigners.

Map the Bay of Catazar.d: Kahraman proposed, and Madruga seconded, a Senate motion to map the Bay of Catazar, supplying Imperial fleets with the resources needed to explore the waters and create an Imperial map. The motion passed in Winter 381YE with an upkeep of 50 Thrones. It created an opportunity for fleet captains to contribute to a special project. That project was completed after the Winter Solstice, when the new map of the Bay of Catazar was finished, with details of the map and the territories surveyed recorded separately.

t.Bay of Catazar: The then-uncontrolled Bay was the subject of the Imperial survey, with fleet captains contributing to an expedition that produced a completed map of its waters after the Winter Solstice.

Poor boy.d: Rico i Matra i Riqueza, a clam diver near Calvos Sound, found an ugly green pearl holding the equivalent of thirty mana crystals, usable only all at once as the sole power for a Spring ritual; he would seek the Grandmaster of the Golden Pyramid. The vate Meri Sixstep searched for remaining Pages of Constellations for 'the Bound King'. A merrow captain of 'the House of the Sixth Wind' salvaged a wrecked ship of the Freeborn Storm that had fled Atalaya, renamed it the Storm Reborn and sought the Freeborn egregores' help to auction it as a non-military vessel equal to a level four fleet. Envoys of Magician-Prince Matvei Kobarid sought Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato's help to auction star jewels.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel attack that destroyed the Atalaya Shipyards and the Freeborn Storm is the backdrop to the salvaged ship, which had slipped their blockade before being wrecked.
n.The League: Jarmish merchants in Tassato brokered the Kobarid envoys' visit, and the envoys hoped Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato would find them a venue and provide security for their star-jewel auction, offering League magicians access to rare enchanted talismans.

t.Tassato: Jarmish merchants based in Tassato arranged for the nephews and nieces of Magician-Prince Matvei Kobarid to visit the Empire on official business to sell enchanted jewellery.

Rebuild Aleksandra's Watch.d: Proposed by the senator for Karsk and seconded by the senator for Reikos, the motion called for construction work at Aleksandra's Watch, a fortress in Karsk. It passed the Senate at the Winter Solstice 381YE with a cost of 20 Thrones. After the summit, Magnus Anatolyvich Prochnost provided the full 20 Thrones, and the reconstruction work was set to be undertaken.

n.Varushka: Varushka saw a fortress in one of its territories restored, with the motion brought by its Karsk senator and funded by Magnus Anatolyvich Prochnost.

t.Karsk: Aleksandra's Watch, a fortress in Karsk, was to undergo reconstruction work once the 20 Thrones had been provided.

Rebuild the Colossus of Sarvos.d: The motion called for the repair of damage inflicted on the Colossus of Sarvos. The work was costed at 8 wains of white granite and 16 crowns, with three months needed to complete it. Shauni di Vergo, bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, announced the project and provided the full 8 wains of white granite and 16 crowns after the Winter Solstice 381YE. With the materials and money supplied, reconstruction work on the Colossus was to be undertaken.

n.The League: A Leaguer landmark in one of the nation's cities was set to be restored, with Shauni di Vergo supplying the granite and crowns for the work.

t.Sarvos: Reconstruction of the damaged Colossus was to begin in Sarvos, with the work expected to take three months once funded.

Research Fire from the Heavens.d: Using the legal power to announce historical research that the Senate has delegated to the office, Ioseph, Minister of Historical Research, commissioned the civil service to research "Fire from the Heavens". This is an enchantment originating from an old coven in Willstone, in the Urizen territory of Redoubt. The page records only the commission, not any findings. A historical research report was due to be delivered to the Minister at the Spring Equinox and published publicly afterwards.

n.Urizen: The research concerns magical lore from Urizen's own past, an enchantment worked by an old coven in one of its territories, and the report may shed light on the nation's magical history.

t.Redoubt: Redoubt, held by Urizen, is the territory where the old coven associated with "Fire from the Heavens" was based, making it the focus of the commissioned research.

r.Redoubt/Willstone: Willstone is named as the home of the old coven whose enchantment, "Fire from the Heavens", is the subject of the research.

Right now.d: The Child of Thunder, crewed only by its captain Artur di Sarvos, rammed the plinth of the Colossus of Sarvos and caused significant damage. Artur asked for clemency from one of three named bishops and was sent to Casinea, to Magistrate Karkovich. Conjunctions were identified to: fight the drowned dead in East Floes; rescue Black Thorns warriors and intercept Grendel looters in Lightsea; counter Druj raiders in Axmure, Lacuve and the Dawnish camps; stop Grendel flanking attacks in Screed and Apulus; and strike Feni warbands in Wood Heath and Birchland. Failures would carry stated penalties to resources or armies. A planned Jotun-related element in Sermersuaq and Segura was dropped.

n.Dawn: Druj skirmishers were harassing Dawnish yeofolk in Semmerholm and poisoning supplies near the Hounds of Glory and Golden Sun camps. Unless stopped, they would cut those armies' casualty-dealing by one tenth.
n.Druj: Druj forces raided Semmerholm, including a relief force from an unknown Tepel heading for the Black Wind army, raiders preying on Lacuve's yeofolk, and Chikad saboteurs near the Dawnish camps.
n.Grendel: Grendel troops were hunting Black Thorns warriors and looting Lightsea. Their elite skirmishers struck the Imperial flanks in Screed, tried to bribe the Wolves of War's mercenaries, and stalked Green Shields patrols in Apulus.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the accused captain Artur di Sarvos was sent to Casinea, where Anvil lies, to face Magistrate Karkovich.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun presence in the west of Sermersuaq was noted, and a planned Wind of Fortune element involving them was withdrawn.
n.Navarr: The Navarr egregores reported that Grendel heavy troops were hunting Black Thorns warriors in Lightsea. A conjunction offered the chance to let them escape and rejoin their army.
n.The Brass Coast: Grendel warbands had ransacked paradors, smiths' warehouses and avocado farms in Lightsea. Heroes could intercept them and recover the loot, with the Brass Coast egregores advising on its return.
n.The League: The League's great Colossus of Sarvos was rammed by one of its own merchant vessels. Grendel agents also tried to buy off the Wolves of War's mercenaries, which threatened to cost that army its mercenaries for a year.
n.The Marches: Feni warbands were ambushing Marcher households in Birchland and stealing food and valuables. The Marches egregores were the contact for a conjunction to strike back.
n.Wintermark: Drowned dead were rising in East Floes and killing those who faced them, and Feni raided halls in Wood Heath. The Wintermark egregores also reported Grendel stalking Green Shields patrols in Apulus.

t.Casinea: Artur di Sarvos was sent under escort to Casinea to surrender to Magistrate Karkovich and seek a bishop's clemency, and an engineer's report on the Colossus was due there too.
t.Hahnmark: Feni warbands were ambushing halls in Wood Heath at dawn and dusk to steal resources, and a conjunction offered a counter-strike.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the vandals posing at the Colossus claimed to be outraged students from Holberg.
t.Madruga: Grendel raiders were sacking Lightsea and pursuing Navarr warriors there, and three conjunctions offered a chance to intervene.
t.Sarvos: The Colossus of Sarvos was rammed and significantly damaged by the merchant ship Child of Thunder, and magistrates were still hunting its escaped crew.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: a planned Wind of Fortune element about the Jotun presence here was withdrawn, with details left to the generals' brief.
t.Semmerholm: Seven conjunctions targeted Druj raiders across Semmerholm. Failure risked reducing local resources by one rank and weakening the Dawnish armies camped there.
t.Sermersuaq: Over three months, unexplained drownings culminated in bloated husks rising from East Floes to attack fishing villages.
t.Spiral: Grendel elites were harrying the Imperial advance in Screed and stalking Green Shields patrols in Apulus, and three conjunctions were identified to stop them.
t.Upwold: Feni bands were raiding Marcher households in Birchland, and a conjunction to Markwood offered a chance to hit them.

r.Hahnmark/Southridge: Mentioned in passing: the snowy hills of Southridge were glimpsed in the in-character story of a Feni attack on Wymarc's Hall.
r.Hahnmark/Wood Heath: Feni warbands were robbing halls in Wood Heath, and a conjunction opened to Bjarwood so fifteen heroes could strike back.
r.Holberg/Holfried: Mentioned in passing: the climber Rihanna recalled once running the roofs and towers of Holfried.
r.Madruga/Lightsea: Conjunctions opened to White Cedars to shield fleeing Black Thorns warriors, and twice to the Plains of Lightsea to intercept Stone Born looters and recover the stolen goods.
r.Semmerholm/Axmure: Druj relief troops were heading for Castle Rock and the Old Wood, and saboteurs were preying on the Ax Glades camps, with four conjunctions offered against them.
r.Semmerholm/Lacuve: Three Druj raiding groups in Lacuve Weald were hitting businesses, supplies and resource shipments, and three conjunctions offered a chance to stop them.
r.Sermersuaq/East Floes: Drowned dead were attacking the settlements of Kuujjuaq, Puvirnituq and Akulivik, each the target of a Friday-evening conjunction, and even the hylje were threatened.
r.Spiral/Apulus: Grendel skirmishers were stalking Green Shields soldiers, and a conjunction to The Bluehaven offered a chance to strike them and learn the fate of lost patrols.
r.Spiral/Screed: Grendel elites were harassing the Iron Helms and suborning Wolves of War mercenaries, with conjunctions to Calvar Field and the Gethern Expanse offered to stop them.
r.Upwold/Birchland: Feni warbands were ambushing Birchland households for loot, and a conjunction to Markwood offered fifteen heroes a chance to strike them.

Root hog, or die.d: With the Navarr steadings emptied by the Jotun, and the Jotun withdrawn westward and smashing their totems, nobody was guarding the Liathaven vallorn. It surged through Westwood and Liath's Heart and threatened to consume West Ranging by the Spring Equinox, which would also swallow the northern end of the Paths of Lan Thúven. Imperial spies warned of the danger. Stopping the surge offered a chance to weaken the vallorn enough for a later strike into Westwood. Meanwhile, mists carried black seeds into Bregasland, where they yielded vital honey. The Quiet Step, the Tusks and the Bounders blunted the expansion, so West Ranging was not infested and the seeds, with their Spring vis, ceased.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Lord Merbrid the Stork supported the Liathaven spy network, and Dawn's Astolat and Semmerholm were noted as having suffered minor miasma during the earlier Brocéliande surge.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj withdrawal from Elerael in 379YE was cited as the trigger for the earlier Brocéliande vallorn surge.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Reikos was listed among territories whose restored trods draw the vallorn's power away, and Casinea was noted as having felt minor miasma during the 379YE surge.
n.Jotun: The Jotun had driven the Navarr out of Liathaven and then withdrawn westward, smashing their totems and leaving the vallorn unguarded. They were also seen as a risk to Imperial forces engaging it, given how close Hordalant lies.
n.Navarr: With their steadings in Liathaven emptied and the Black Thorns unable to respond, the Navarr faced a vallorn surge that threatened the Paths of Lan Thúven. The Quiet Step helped blunt it, a struggle that also opened a possible chance to strike into Westwood later.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: Holberg was listed among territories restored to the trods, and Magdelena Alanga Di Sarvos and Kaspar Yakovich von Holberg supported the spy network.
n.The Marches: Bregasland's farms gained vital honey from vallorn seeds carried on the mists, and the Marcher armies the Tusks and the Bounders helped blunt the expansion, which ended that windfall.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Karsk was listed among territories restored to the trods, Maarit supported the spy network, and a Varushkan scout appears in the opening story.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: cited as having suffered minor miasma overspill during the 379YE Brocéliande surge.
t.Bregasland: Mists bearing black seeds drifted along the trod into Bregasland's marshes, and every farm harvested the equivalent of a piece of vital honey. This ended once the vallorn was kept out of West Ranging.
t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: its vallorn's 379YE expansion into Elerael was cited as the closest recent precedent.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: cited as having suffered minor miasma overspill during the 379YE Brocéliande surge.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: listed as restored to the web of trods that drain the vallorn's power.
t.Hordalant: Mentioned in passing: its nearness to Liathaven raised the risk of Jotun attacks on Imperial forces fighting the vallorn.
t.Karsk: Mentioned in passing: listed as restored to the web of trods that drain the vallorn's power.
t.Liathaven: The unguarded vallorn surged out of its heart towards West Ranging, but Imperial armies blunted the expansion and kept the territory's remaining land free of it.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: listed as restored to the web of trods that drain the vallorn's power.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: cited as having suffered minor miasma overspill during the 379YE Brocéliande surge.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: the Black Thorns pushed through the Barrens with the aid of the orcs of the Great Forest to deal with the 379YE surge.

r.Brocéliande/Elerael: Mentioned in passing: the vallorn's 379YE expansion into Elerael after the Druj withdrew was cited as a precedent.
r.Liathaven/Liath's Heart: A surge of power rippled through Liath's Heart, raising the dead and stirring its vallornspawn. The core itself remained too strong to attack.
r.Liathaven/Liath's Ring: The seed-bearing fog travelled north along the trod from Liath's Ring to Bregasland, and a Sentinel Gate conjunction opened onto Mournstead here at the Solstice.
r.Liathaven/West Ranging: The vallorn threatened to consume West Ranging and swallow the northern end of the Paths of Lan Thúven, but Imperial forces blunted the expansion and it was not infested.
r.Liathaven/Western Scout: Mentioned in passing: conquering it was named as one way to support a later attack into Westwood.
r.Liathaven/Westwood: The vallorn surged through Westwood. Halting its expansion offered a possible chance for the Navarr to strike here later and permanently clear the region.

Sing your name.d: The Heirs of Lepidus, stewards of the dead who recover lore on paragons and exemplars, showed that the Silent Sentinel's ancient foundations match the Sentinel's known towers and are the largest of them. Highborn researching the Sentinel were repeatedly attacked by an unidentified 'red shadow'; nobody was killed. The General Assembly mandated Rhesa, Exarch of the Scions of Ravensfell, to consecrate the site in the name of Vigilance. For roughly a year, until shortly before Winter Solstice 382YE, new or improved white granite fortifications need a fifth less granite. The Senate voted to build the tower of the Sentinel, a sinecure and pilgrimage site expected to be finished shortly before Spring Equinox 382YE.

n.Highguard: The discovery centres on a Highborn fortress and Highborn scholars, who alone have faced the red shadow's attacks, and Highborn patrons funded the Heirs; the Highborn national assembly was suggested as a possible appointer of the new sinecure.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the School of Epistemology in Tassato is noted as having worked with the Heirs of Lepidus on the earlier recovery of lore about Berechiah.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: benefactors of Reumah's Redoubt are named among the patrons who funded the Heirs of Lepidus.

t.Casinea: The Silent Sentinel in Casinea was truly consecrated as the likely home of the Sentinel and became a site of Vigilance pilgrimage, with the Senate commissioning a grand beacon tower there due shortly before Spring Equinox 382YE.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: the benefactors of Reumah's Redoubt are cited as providing significant backing to the Heirs of Lepidus.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: Tassato's School of Epistemology is credited with helping the Heirs recover and publish information on the exemplar Berechiah in late 380YE.

Sowing on the mountains.d: In Mieriada, floods at Wendell's Hope exposed an ossuary of pre-Imperial Varushkan heroes who fell fighting the Thule. Its wise ones proposed a great work of monument and shrine, costing 30 wains of white granite, 10 of weirwood and 10 Thrones, that would add 50 Synod votes and 25 liao. In Brez, a tempest jade cave at Bredavoi could become a mine yielding 20 ingots a season, but its deep tunnels hide dark spirits. In Opascari, a Terunael orichalcum mine on the Traveller could be restored. In Suvretz, the plans and foundations of the unfinished Irontooth Keep were found, and koboldi offered to help build it. All four lapsed at the Spring Equinox 384YE.

n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the Silent Sentinel in Casinea and Remember Exile in Reikos are named as the fortifications Irontooth Keep might rival.
n.Navarr: The Navarr are said to be very interested in why a Terunael outpost stands on the Traveller in Opascari, and reopening the pass might reveal more for them to study.
n.Thule: The Thule embassy was reportedly damaged by a rockslide, the Wendell's Hope monument would be built partly as a warning to them, and they may claim the reopened Sungold Pass mine if the Empire does not.
n.Varushka: Varushka gained the chance to honour its ancient dead with a pilgrimage site and to commission new mines and a great fortress, with the titles that would follow, in its storm-wracked northern territories.

t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: the Silent Sentinel in Casinea is cited as a fortification Irontooth Keep might rival.
t.Miekarova: Floods at Wendell's Hope uncovered an ossuary of ancient Varushkan heroes, and a proposed great work there would draw more pilgrims and grant Synod votes and liao to Varushkan-led congregations in Miekarova.
t.Otkodov: The storm raged through the mountains bordering Otkodov, whose tunnels may connect to Brez and whose warped forest creatures sometimes raid Suvretz.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: Remember Exile in Reikos is cited as a fortification Irontooth Keep might rival.
t.Volodmartz: The storm revealed three opportunities in Volodmartz: a tempest jade mine in Brez, a Terunael orichalcum mine in Opascari, and the unfinished Irontooth Keep in Suvretz.

r.Miekarova/Mieriada: At Wendell's Hope on the Coldmere, wise ones proposed turning the newly exposed ossuary into a monument and shrine to Courage, visible from the nearby Thule embassy.
r.Otkodov/Sküld: Thule armies have three times marched out of Sküld into Suvretz, and the Sungold Pass ruins can be reached as easily from Sküld as from Volodmartz.
r.Volodmartz/Brez: Wagon raiders found a rich tempest jade seam in a cave below Bredavoi peak, which could be commissioned as a mine with a Foreman title, though dark spirits lurk in the deep tunnels.
r.Volodmartz/Opascari: An avalanche on the Traveller uncovered a Terunael orichalcum mine with heat-holding mithril designs, which could be restored with a Warden of the Sungold Pass title before the Thule claim it.
r.Volodmartz/Suvretz: Floods revealed the foundations and original plans of Irontooth Keep, a great fortress to guard against the Thule and Otkodov's creatures, which koboldi were eager to help build.

Talking sailor.d: In the weeks before the Winter Solstice 381YE, attacks on traders crossing the Bay rose, with pirates aided by shark-like creatures likely to be heralds of the Mother-of-Wrecks. Unless the situation changed, trading fleets from Tassato, Sarvos, the Brass Coast, Highguard and Urizen faced a one-rank production penalty. Asavean, Sarcophan and Jarmish ships were left alone. The Senate could have let Imperial ships fly those nations' colours, at a diplomatic cost. It could also fund a 50-Throne project for captains and civil service cartographers to chart the Bay's coasts and territories. The Senate voted to map the Bay, and many captains took part. The Grendel continued to raid Imperial shipping.

n.Grendel: Grendel pirates of the Broken Shore, spurred by Siakha's growing influence and left loosely organised by the defence of the fishing fleet, stepped up their raids on Imperial traders and continued raiding after the Solstice.
n.Highguard: Highguard's trading fleets faced a one-rank production penalty from increased Grendel piracy if they traded through the Bay in the coming season.
n.The Brass Coast: Brass Coast trading fleets risked the piracy penalty, while their corsairs, sworn to protect Imperial shipping, were stretched by the Grendel invasion of Madruga. Their long family knowledge of the Bay made them obvious partners in mapping it.
n.The League: League fleets based in Tassato and Sarvos faced reduced production from Grendel piracy if they engaged in trade through the Bay.
n.Urizen: Urizeni trading fleets were among those facing a one-rank production penalty from the surge in Grendel piracy.

t.Bay of Catazar: The Bay was dominated militarily by the Grendel armada and plagued by Siakha-backed pirates. The Senate voted to fund a concerted effort to chart its coastline, territories and features.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel invasion of Madruga is cited as a problem distracting the Brass Coast corsairs from protecting shipping.
t.Sarvos: Fleets based in Sarvos faced a one-rank production penalty if they traded through the pirate-infested Bay in the coming season.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the ongoing campaign in Spiral is noted as a reason the Military Council was unprepared for any strike against the Broken Shore.
t.Tassato: Fleets based in Tassato faced a one-rank production penalty if they engaged in trade while Grendel piracy surged.

The flood and the storm.d: After six months in which no Spring regio could be drawn upon, the realm's magic returned with unusual force, blamed by some on a Fountain–Stallion conjunction and by suspicious goetic magicians on a primal Spring power. Magicians working Spring rituals through a regio could embrace the surge for added strength at the risk of traumatic wounds. Three opportunities arose: a mithril-inlaid Moonwell in Hahnmark, a garden sinecure at ruined Evenstar in Redoubt, and a granite-and-weirwood great work over the Eye of Serenael in Miaren. The Senate commissioned Seren's Whispering Garden. Meanwhile the Heart of the Tempest in Miekarova began to spread before falling quiet after the Solstice, as the flood subsided and the remaining opportunities lapsed.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel raiders are recalled as having sacked Evenstar in Winter 380YE, enslaving its healers and using its regio to unleash sea magic against Redoubt.
n.Navarr: Navarr magicians, masters of herding Spring magic, gained a great work when the Senate voted to build Seren's Whispering Garden over the Eye of Serenael to channel its power along Miaren's trods to the nation's steadings.
n.Urizen: The Urizen identified the ruined spire of Evenstar as seething with Spring power and were offered the chance to raise a sinecure providing crystal mana and healing herbs, appointable by their senators, though only the Miaren project is recorded as taken up before the flood subsided.
n.Varushka: Varushkans faced the slow expansion of the Heart of the Tempest, whose plant-like creatures were reported spiriting away lone travellers, until the woods became quiescent after the Winter Solstice.
n.Wintermark: Steinr runesmiths Hurik and Manun offered to inlay the ancient Spring well near Valashal with mithril, creating a Moonwell Runewarden title yielding vital honey, possibly appointed by the Wintermark senators; it is not recorded as built before the opportunity lapsed.

t.Hahnmark: The traditional Steinr fertility well near Valashal filled with sweet, treacle-thick water, offering a brief chance to build a mithril Moonwell yielding vital honey each season.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: the Hahnmark well stands not far from the edges of Kallavesa's Rundhal Marsh.
t.Miaren: Surging power from the Eye of Serenael caused bursts of wild growth and weather near Seren, and the Senate voted to build Seren's Whispering Garden to channel it, promising crystal mana to herb gardens and herbs to mana sites across the territory.
t.Miekarova: The Heart of the Tempest began expanding a few paces a week, its strange denizens venturing beyond it amid fears of an unknown sovereign, before growing quiet after the Solstice.
t.Redoubt: The ruined hospital-spire of Evenstar burst into a flowering memorial garden bearing crystalline mana fruit, offering a fleeting chance to build a sinecure for an Evenstar Defender.

r.Hahnmark/Valasmark: South-west of Valashal, the rune-carved Spring well turned thick and sweet, and runesmiths proposed a mithril-inlaid Moonwell producing a seasonal bucket of vital honey.
r.Kallavesa/Rundhal Marsh: Mentioned in passing: the marsh's edges serve only as a landmark for the location of the Hahnmark well.
r.Miaren/Serenael: The Eye of Serenael on the outskirts of Seren became a troubling fountainhead of Spring energy, prompting the Senate to commission Seren's Whispering Garden over it.
r.Miekarova/Mieriada: The Heart of the Tempest in Mieriada spread slowly and its plant-like creatures were reported abducting travellers, until the forest became quiescent in the weeks after the Solstice.
r.Redoubt/Naris: At Evenstar on Naris's southern coast, overgrown herb gardens and mana-bearing fruit offered a brief chance to harness the regio with a web of mithril and weirwood.

This land is your land.d: The Conclave interdicted Rivers Run Red and Mountain Remembers Its Youth, though the Senate did not remove them from Imperial lore. Nedry Galest, General of the Tusks, went to the wicker man to atone for the curses. The Senate commissioned fortifications in Greensward and Freemoor but rejected one for Southmoor. The Mournwold stays stable if those are built and the interdictions hold for five years. Lifting either would be disastrous. Many Whittle folk returned home, still shunned and still devoted to Hatred. Three further opportunities were offered: Richard of Holberg's mithril menhirs, a third fortification, and granting the Singing Caves to the Marches. The Senate later voted itself a power of relinquishment, and construction began on the two fortifications.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Mournwolders blame Dawn's senators, without much evidence, for the Senate's failure to remove the two curses from Imperial lore.
n.Imperial Orcs: A rumour that the Imperial Orcs might give up their own Bourse resource so that the Singing Caves could go to the Marches was seen as an exceptional gesture. The Constitutional Court set out a lawful route for doing so, and the Senate later created the power of relinquishment. Imperial Orc preachers were also invited to preach the Way to the freed thralls of the Mourn.
n.Jotun: The Jotun had fled the Mournwold. The new fortifications are meant to stop them ever retaking it, and their former orc thralls were invited to send leaders to Anvil.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: a revived market town at Sarcombe could renew trade with the Navarr once they retake Liathaven.
n.The League: Mournwolders contemptuously see handing the Singing Caves to the Bourse as giving them to the League. The Marcher enclave in Tassato prospers even as many Whittle folk leave it. Leaguers Ricardo de Tassato and Cesare Enzo Di Trivento were praised by the Marcher Assembly.
n.The Marches: Nedry Galest's sacrifice and the Empire's concessions renewed Marcher loyalty and pride in the Mournwold. The Marcher Assembly still struggles to persuade a grudge-holding people of the difference between the false virtue of Hate and everyday hatred. The Marches could gain its first national Bourse seat if the Singing Caves were granted to it.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's decision to fund a new monastery in Overton, and the Winterfolk's Senate motion for a memorial there, were well received, though folk want a Mournwolder put in charge of the monastery.

t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: the returning Whittle folk are described as 'as cold as a Bregasland eel'.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: only through the name of the architect Richard (Dicky) of Holberg, who designed the proposed menhir network for the Mourn.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: trade through Sarcombe could resume with the Navarr once they have retaken Liathaven from the Jotun.
t.Mournwold: The territory's mood shifted from open rebellion to cautious patience. Stability depends on the commissioned fortifications being built and the two curses staying interdicted for five years. Menhirs, a third fortification and the Singing Caves remain open opportunities.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: the Constitutional Court said relinquishment would not be allowed by extraordinary motion, as had happened with Skarsind.
t.Tassato: More than half the remaining Whittle folk left Tassato to return home. The younger Marchers who stayed form a prospering enclave, 'Little Mournwold', that increasingly takes on Tassatan ways.

r.Mournwold/Freemoor: The Senate commissioned a fortification in Freemoor, and construction has since begun.
r.Mournwold/Greensward: The Senate commissioned a fortification in Greensward, and construction has since begun.
r.Mournwold/Southmoor: The Senate rejected a fortification for Southmoor, but locals hope it will reconsider and favour the ruined mining town of Sarcombe, on the foundations of the Jotun fort Hillstop. That could revive the town as a chartered market and trade hub.

What did the deep say?.d: A sailor, sole survivor of a wrecked merchant crew, carried Siakha's message: a champion would meet the Archmage of Spring in the Hall of Worlds, not under parley, and the civil service warned this could be dangerous. Ephisis accepted parley with the Autumn Archmage to discuss trade, bringing other interested traders. Janon's troubadour-emissary accepted parley with Archmage of Night Elyssiathain Endsmeet to discuss boons and asked for Kahendrin Wordsmith. Barien will attend Archmage Solomon's feast with four Summer nobles and reward the best troubadours with a token. Tharim, tired of repeated requests, sent the herald Shackle; agents of his court will discuss its nature under parley and may bring 'gifts' for the Conclave.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: in the sailor's tale, a Grendel ship sank Cinque di Sarvos's vessel decades ago and left its crew in shark-infested water.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: a bosun's mate from Hahnmark, Hervis Rohansson, is recalled as one of the shipwrecked sailors killed by sharks in a story.

t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: the doomed sailor Hervis Rohansson in Cinque's tale is said to have come from Hahnmark.

You know the night.d: The Iron Helms, raised in Spring 381YE and famed for cruelty, were unleashed in the Mournwold with effective but disturbing results. Wintermark and the Freeborn had already passed mandates urging their soldiers to shun the Helms. Dawn, Highguard, Navarr and Urizen sided with Varushka. After Gralka's judgement, upheld 36 to 0, the Imperial Orc assembly could shun the Helms or permanently change the Summer Storm from relentless to heroic. It unanimously refused the Summer Storm change. The Varushkan assembly sent Bogdan Bogdanovich with a mandate urging all its soldiers to embrace their heritage. All Varushkan armies thereby stood with the Iron Helms, sharing their penalties when fighting alongside Wintermark and the Brass Coast, and each general gained one chance to update their army's quality.

n.Dawn: Dawn was counted among the nations standing with the Iron Helms and Varushka in the dispute over their cruel tactics.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: Empress Varkula's remark that high-minded ideals last only until the Druj are about to burn your house down is cited by Varushkans.
n.Highguard: Highguard was named among the nations that chose to stand with Varushka and the Iron Helms.
n.Imperial Orcs: Gralka's judgement condemning the Iron Helms' cruelty passed 36 to 0, opening mandates to shun the Helms and to make the Summer Storm heroic. The assembly unanimously refused to change the Summer Storm's quality.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Varushkans dismissed the Marches and Wintermark as nations bordering the Jotun that have never faced an enemy really trying.
n.Navarr: The Navarr sided with Varushka and were inspired to pass a mandate adopting similar tactics to the Iron Helms.
n.The Marches: The Marches were among the first nations to oppose the Iron Helms' tactics, drawing Varushkan scorn as high-minded farmers and hunters.
n.Urizen: Urizen narrowly backed Varushka, reportedly thanks to Zeno, and was inspired to pass a mandate adopting similar tactics.
n.Varushka: Varushka's assembly sent Bogdan Bogdanovich to urge all its soldiers to embrace their heritage, so every Varushkan army now stands with the Iron Helms and shares their penalties alongside Wintermark and the Brass Coast. Each general also gained a single chance to update their army's quality.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark had already enacted a mandate shunning the Iron Helms, and after Varushka's mandate all Varushkan armies now suffer penalties when fighting alongside Wintermark armies.

t.Mournwold: The Iron Helms were first unleashed in the Mournwold, where their cruel methods proved as effective as they were hard for many to stomach.
